## E-2026-07-24-GEOSTAR-LOCUS — is GeometricStar's density-invariant true-3D residual caused by `extractGeometricStar` conforming to the WRONG locus (straight full-height fold columns instead of the staggered/zigzag strapwork ramp), and does emitting the MEASURED loci close it toward 0.01mm? [BUILD+PROVE; src edit `FeatureLineGraph.ts`, flag-gated default-OFF byte-identical; env-gated probes PF_GSLOCUS / PF_GSLOCI]

**HYPOTHESIS (as tasked, falsifiable).** The shipped `extractGeometricStar` emits straight full-height verticals at `u=(k+0.5)/N`, which is wrong for odd rows (row-parity stagger) and misses the strapwork ramp entirely; the mesh therefore refines the wrong locus, chords the real ridge, and leaves the density-invariant residual (E-2026-07-23-GEOSTAR-SEAM-LOCK MAX 0.684, `hitBudget`, worst facets maxEdge 1.52mm vs hMin 0.04mm). Emitting the TRUE loci as `general-curve` polylines into the local-CDT insertion engine moves the worst facet off the ridge and drops the MAX toward 0.01.

**KILL-CRITERION (pre-registered, in the probe header before any arm ran).** CONFIRMED-MECHANISM iff exact-loci MAX ≤ 0.5×legacy MAX **and** the top-10 worst facets stop straddling the ramp. CLOSED iff MAX ≤ 0.01. REFUTED iff MAX ≥ 0.9×legacy. PARTIAL otherwise.

**VERDICT: PARTIAL — mechanism CONFIRMED and large (legacy MAX 0.734 → 0.120, off-seam 0.734 → 0.017, p99 0.0946 → 0.0073, over-0.1mm 0.921% → 0.000%), but NOT CLOSED to 0.01; the second leg (worst facets leave the ramp) FIRED NEGATIVE — they stay on the ramp and simply relocate to the u-seam clip band. Two premises of the task were MEASURED FALSE and are corrected below.**

**LOCUS CLASSIFICATION (measured on `rOuterGeometricStar`, PROD dims H120/Rb45/Rt70/expn1.1, registry defaults; `_gsLocus.test.ts`).** Verdicts by ε→0 behaviour of the value gap vs the one-sided slope jump (ε ∈ {1e-3…1e-6}):

| locus | formula | measured verdict | magnitude |
|---|---|---|---|
| row-parity STAGGER | `u_fold(row,j)=(j+0.5−(row%2)·shift)/N` | **EXACT** — translation identity `dStrap_row1(u) ≡ dStrap_row0(u+shift/N)` holds to **2.1e-15**; but **DORMANT at registry defaults** (`gs_shift` default = **0** ⇒ rows 0/1 crossings agree bit-for-bit; shift=1 ⇒ a full sector ⇒ identity again) | Δu = shift/N |
| fold ridge `u=(k+0.5)/N` | `p.x=abs(a·N/4)` fold | **C1-KINK, but only over 2.7% of each row** — sharp bands (slope jump > 1 mm/mm-arc) at t∈[0.1127,0.1161]∪[0.1339,0.1373] in row 0; the slope jump is EXACTLY 0 on the far plateau (relief identically zero) and 0 at v=0 | peak 10.33 mm/mm-arc ⇒ the shipped `verticalLine(u,0,1)` is **97.3% NON-FEATURE** |
| strap ramp `dStrap∈[0,edge]` | level curves of `abs(dLine)−gap` | **C1-SMOOTH, NOT a cliff** — value gap AND slope jump both →0 (smoothstep has zero derivative at both ends ⇒ C2-discontinuous only). It is merely very **STEEP** | Δr **2.235mm over 0.659mm of arc** (3.39 mm/mm); a flat facet needs arc ≤ **0.05mm** for ≤0.01mm chord (h=0.125→0.051, h=0.0625→0.014, h=0.05→0.0091) |
| row boundary `t=k/(layers·zoom)` | `vFade=1−abs(v)^4` → 0 | **SMOOTH — NOT a crease** (a plausible candidate, measured false): `shape` is already identically 0 before abs(v)→1 (max p.x 0.785 < the 0.901 required), so value gap and slope jump both vanish | nothing to emit |

All three worst facets of E-2026-07-23-GEOSTAR-SEAM-LOCK (u 0.7809/0.6552/0.7815) sit **inside the ramp band**, ~0.25 sector-cells from the nearest legacy fold column ⇒ "wrong locus" CONFIRMED as the diagnosis, with the correct locus being the RAMP (the user's "zigzag" = the chevron level curve), not the row stagger.

**EVIDENCE (GeometricStar, PROD dims H120/Rb45/Rt70/expn1.1, registry defaults; engine = `buildConformingWall` local-CDT insertion, nRing256/resU-T128/minEdge0.02/gradeRatio2/budgetMode cap; ONE lever = the feature-line set; ONE ruler both meshes = `perFaceTrue3DSag` lifted with the exact `buildRadiusFn`):**

| arm | L | maxSag | tris | **true-3D MAX** | MAX off-seam | p99 | p99.9 | over0.01 | over0.1 | nonMan | %<20° |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| none (control) | 11 | 0.05 | 300,368 | **0.73357** | — | 0.1304 | 0.3391 | 26.96%* | 1.755% | 0 | 4.1 |
| **legacy (shipped extractor)** | 11 | 0.05 | 551,680 | **0.73357** | 0.73357 | 0.09463 | 0.29188 | 12.56% | 0.921% | 0 | 2.5 |
| exact loci, rampSteps 1 | 9 | 0.05 | 335,360 | 0.30451 | — | 0.03803 | 0.04148 | — | 0.011% | 0 | 31.6 |

(* = scored with the default `preFilterMm` 0.02, so every value ≤0.02 is an UPPER BOUND, not a projection; the decisive rows were re-scored at preFilter 0.004.)

1. **The SHIPPED extractor is a MAX no-op.** legacy MAX 0.73357 is *bit-identical* to the no-lines control — the 8 full-height fold columns buy some p99 (0.130→0.095) and nothing at all at the worst facet, because 97.3% of each column is provably not a feature and the real locus is ~0.25 sector-cells away.
2. **The measured loci deliver 6.1× MAX / 43× off-seam MAX / 13× p99**, at 3.4× the triangles, watertight (nonMan 0 by index), with over-0.1mm eliminated (0.921% → 0.000%). **The RENDER agrees with the metric** (true-3D heatmap montage): the legacy mesh's error IS the chevron ZIGZAG, drawn in red/yellow; the exact-loci mesh is uniformly green (0.00% >0.03 vs 4.83%).
3. **The residual after conforming is NOT a geometric floor — it is three named, separable mechanisms** (`runDiag` + per-class worst-facet loci):
   (a) **u-SEAM CLIP — 0.11998, density-INVARIANT** (identical at L11 and L12: same facet, maxEdge 0.5631mm unchanged). `clipFeaturesToBox(features, uMargin=1.5/2^featureLevel, tMargin)` strips the feature lines in a band at u=0/1, and the chevron runs nearly parallel to the seam there. MEASURED: at the worst facet the nearest emitted line point goes **3.5e-4 → 1.6e-3 after the clip (CLIPPED AWAY)**, while every non-seam probe is unchanged by the clip. After rampSteps 4 the entire top-10 is this class (10/10 at-seam, vs 2/10 before).
   (b) **RAMP-INTERIOR — 0.0349, FIXED here.** The two bounding level curves leave the band's middle 2–3 quadtree cells unrefined (band Δu 2.25e-3 vs cell 4.9e-4 at L11), invisible to the band-limited sizing field; subdividing the band (`geoStarRampSteps`) removes this class from the tail entirely.
   (c) **smooth-cone chord — 0.0203 → 0.01715.** The worst off-seam facets at rampSteps 4 were 3.4mm facets on the *featureless* cone (dStrap 0.55–0.81, no relief): a pure `maxSagMm` knob, density-responsive by construction.
4. **The refiner is BLIND to the ramp because its sampler is a 512×512 bilinear grid.** `styleSampler`'s grid has Δu = 0.57mm of arc ≈ the ENTIRE 0.659mm ramp width, and its own MAX deviation from the exact analytic on GeoStar is **0.62004mm** (1024²: 0.24703, 2048²: 0.08472, 4096²: 0.02492 — clean O(h²), so ≤0.01 would need ~8192² ≈ 268M grid points). That is why the sag-driven quadtree cannot find the ramp on its own, and why ANALYTIC feature lines (which bypass the sampler) are the lever that works. It is also a hard ceiling on any *production* mesh whose vertex POSITIONS come from that sampler — the fidelity numbers above lift (u,t) exactly (lab convention), so they isolate the mesher's density decisions.

**TASK-PREMISE CORRECTIONS (both measured, both material).** (i) The row-parity stagger is real and the formula is exact, but `gs_shift` defaults to **0** in `registry.ts`, so the stagger is DORMANT at production defaults and **cannot** be the cause of the 0.684 residual — the extractor bug it represents is LATENT (fires only for `gs_shift>0`) and is fixed here under the flag. (ii) The strap edges are **not** C0/near-C0 cliffs; they are C1-smooth STEEP ramps, so the fix is density-on-the-right-locus, not discontinuity alignment — which is exactly why the two prior dedicated-graph experiments (E-2026-07-19-GEOSTAR-CHEVRON-CONFORM, E-2026-07-22 crease-conform) failed: they inserted the same curves as HARD constraints into engines that could not embed them (80.7% recovery) or that traded chord for slivers.

**REGRESSION GATES.** `FeatureLineGraph.test.ts` **49/49** (the 2 legacy GeoStar pins UNCHANGED + 5 new: exact-loci emission with `groundTruthCount` 8→72, exact stagger at shift 0/0.5/1, every ramp point on its level curve to <2e-3, zero-relief honest-empty, and an explicit FLAG-OFF byte-identical pin that also asserts `surfaceFidelityExact:true` does NOT switch it). `eslint --max-warnings=0` clean on every edited file; `tsc --noEmit` emits **zero** errors mentioning the edited files. Conforming suite: 638 passed / 2 failed — `AnalyticCurvatureFloor.test.ts` (SpiralRidges closed form) and `MultiCurveCellPolicy.test.ts` (fanRepair boundary-edge delta), both **PRE-EXISTING / concurrent-workstream**: neither has any runtime dependency on the edited file (AnalyticCurvatureFloor imports only `types`/`profile`; MultiCurveCellPolicy reaches `FeatureLineGraph` only via `import type`, erased at runtime), and the concurrent workstream has `ConstrainedCellTriangulator.ts` uncommitted in exactly the fanRepair area.

**PRODUCTION SAFETY.** All new behaviour is behind `ExtractOpts.geoStarExactLoci` (dev lever `__pfGeoStarLoci`), DELIBERATELY **not** wired to the shippable `surfaceFidelityExact` flag — pinned by test. Flag off ⇒ the identical 8 full-height `vertical-crease` lines, `groundTruthCount` 8.

**RECOMMENDATION.** (a) **KEEP the corrected extractor flag-gated** — it is the honest locus map and the only lever measured to move GeoStar's MAX; do NOT flip it onto `surfaceFidelityExact` yet (the sliver cost is real: %<20° 2.5 → 25.6, minAngle 1.4° → 0.4°). (b) **Next experiment = the u-SEAM CLIP**, the sole remaining density-invariant class: emit the seam-crossing chevron as a *seam-continuous* pair (snap the clipped endpoints to u=0 and u=1 at matching t) so `clipFeaturesToBox` no longer opens a hole, or shrink `uMargin` on the periodic (non-shared) u boundary the way `onSameSeamLine` did for the region kernel in E-2026-07-23-GEOSTAR-SEAM-LOCK. Predicted result: MAX 0.120 → ~0.017 (the measured off-seam value). (c) **Then the sampler**: 0.01mm end-to-end also requires replacing `styleSampler`'s 512² bilinear grid with exact analytic evaluation (`buildAnalyticRadiusFn`) — measured floor 0.62mm at defaults; same "grid-bound is the wrong surface" meta-fix as the analytic-scoring lever. (d) **Cheatsheet correction**: the settled map's "EXCLUDE — risers (…GeometricStar…): conforming HURTS" is REFUTED *for this engine* — conforming to the CORRECT loci helps by 6.1× MAX / 43× off-seam. What hurt was conforming to the WRONG loci (the legacy columns) or inserting the right ones as unembeddable hard constraints.

## E-2026-07-23-GEOSTAR-SEAM-LOCK — is GeometricStar's production-emitter `nonMan 3` a rim-pin SEAM-WELD defect, and does welding it + de-capping close the true-3D MAX 0.697 → ≤0.01? [BUILD+PROVE; src edit `regionMetric.ts`, flag-gated default-OFF byte-identical; env-gated probe PF_GSSEAM_*]

**HYPOTHESIS (as tasked, falsifiable).** The E-2026-07-23-HARDCARD `nonMan 3` is a rim-pin u=1→u=0 SEAM-WELD defect in `metricMeshToOuterWall` (a seam/rim vertex duplicated instead of shared ⇒ crack + stray facet); welding it by index (nonMan 0, boundary = 2·nRing) plus a raised budget closes the localized MAX 0.697 (p99 0.00488) to ≤0.01mm true-3D at production density.

**KILL-CRITERION (pre-registered).** SEAM-WELD CONFIRMED iff the 3 non-manifold edges lie ON the periodic seam (u≈0/1) or the rim rows (t≈0/1) AND a weld/collection fix drives nonMan 3→0. REFUTED iff they are INTERIOR. MAX CLOSED iff `measureProjectorMax`/`perFaceTrue3DSag` MAX ≤0.01 at prod density.

**VERDICT: seam-weld hypothesis REFUTED (nonMan is INTERIOR + a ruler artifact); a DIFFERENT, REAL seam defect found and FIXED (the seam-refinement LOCK); MAX NOT closed — honest residual 0.684, mechanism = budget-starved interior under-refinement.**

**EVIDENCE (GeometricStar, PROD dims H120/Rb45/Rt70/expn1.1, `buildRegionOuterWall` nRing2048/tol0.003/hMin0.04/hMax1/sizeRes128/chordTol0.003/maxPoints5M — the EXACT HARDCARD config; ~10M tris, 5M-vert cap HIT):**

| arm | tris | true-3D MAX | p99 | nonMan (pos-weld 1e-4) | nonMan (RAW index) | boundary | rings |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pre-fix (reproduction) | 9,995,860 | **0.696835** | 0.01393 | **3** | **0** | **4096** = 2·nRing | 2048 / 2048 |
| post-fix (seam unfrozen) | 9,995,376 | **0.684105** | 0.01393 | 3 | **0** | 4096 | 2048 / 2048 |

1. **`nonMan 3` is NOT a seam-weld defect — it is a RULER artifact on an already-watertight mesh.** The 3 edges are **INTERIOR**: u≈0.258088/t≈0.051371 (z6.16, ×2) and u≈0.720835/t≈0.314001 (z37.68), each mult=4 with incident triangles in *coincident pairs*. The packed mesh is **manifold by RAW INDEX (nonMan 0), boundary EXACTLY 4096 = 2·nRing, 0 repeated-index degenerate faces** — i.e. already watertight-by-index with only the two open rims. `auditNonManByIndex` merges vertex pairs **7.0e-5 / 9.3e-5 mm apart** at its 1e-4mm position-weld quantize (min pairwise 3D distance measured in each fold window), collapsing them into mult-4 folds. Seam columns are a clean bijection (**col0 = col1 = 13**).
2. **Two candidate weld fixes REFUTED by measurement.** (a) `RING_EPS` 1e-6→1e-9 (the seam/rim collection band, which collides exactly with `surfaceSmoothing`'s eps=1e-6 interior clamp) is a **no-op**: identical nonMan 3 at identical loci. (b) Post-hoc vertex welding is **HARMFUL** — 3D weld+dedup at 1.5e-4/3e-4mm gave nonMan 3→**18/62** and grew boundary 4096→**4120/4180** (it opened cracks: naive vertex merge violates the link condition); a (u,t) weld at 1e-5 over-merged 12,957 verts → nonMan **4937**.
3. **A REAL, separate seam defect FOUND + FIXED: the seam-refinement LOCK.** `onSameBoundaryLine` locked *all four* patch boundaries from splitting, freezing the periodic u=0/u=1 columns at the SEED resolution (`seedNt+1` = **13** t-stations, ~10mm apart in z) while the interior refined to hMin=0.04mm. Measured consequence (pre-fix): the **worst-20 true-3D facets were ALL at u≈0.0004 / u≈0.9996**, with **maxEdge 1.5–6.5mm (37–160× hMin)** across radSpread 1.0–1.35mm of chevron relief — carrying the entire MAX 0.697. It is **INVARIANT under `maxPoints`** (budget refines the interior, never the locked seam), which explains the HARDCARD 4×-budget step moving MAX only 1.167→0.697. FIX: split the predicate into `onSameRimLine` (t-rows STILL locked ⇒ rings stay exactly nRing) and `onSameSeamLine` (u-columns now splittable), with every seam split **MIRRORED onto both columns** by the new `addSplitPoint` so u=0/u=1 keep an identical t-station set and the weld bijection holds. **PROVEN:** the seam facets are **eliminated from the worst tail** — pre-fix worst-UB top-10 contained 3 seam facets (u≈0.0003 ×2, u≈0.9997 @ub 0.70–0.72); post-fix contains **zero**. Rings 2048/2048, boundary 4096, raw nonMan 0 all preserved.
4. **MAX NOT CLOSED — honest residual 0.684 (−1.8%), and the seam was not the binding constraint.** Post-fix the MAX is carried by an INTERIOR class: u≈0.7809/t≈0.0659 (z7.91, ub 0.991), u≈0.6552/t≈0.3127 (z37.5), u≈0.7815/t≈0.0882. These facets have **maxEdge ≈1.52mm vs hMin 0.04mm (38×)** — they are **UNDER-REFINED, not at the sizing floor and not cliff-limited**. The build reports `hitBudget=true` (refinement aborts mid-round at the 5M-vertex cap), so the residual is **budget-starved under-resolution, NOT a geometric floor**. Tail size: 184,379 facets >0.01mm (1.845%), 973 >0.1mm (0.0097%); p99 0.01393, p99.9 0.0357. Sliver cost unchanged (pctBelow20 5.10%, minAngle 0.000°).

**REGRESSION GATES (all green, post-fix):** `flagOff.byteIdentical` ✓; `regionMetric.test.ts` 7/7 (incl. the RIM-PIN weld test — rings exactly nRing, nonManifold 0, boundary 2·nRing — and the whole-solid assembly smoke: boundary 0, nonManifold 0); `dsFeatureEdges.test.ts` 10/10 (incl. DS seam-symmetry + DS rim-pin dispatch); `smoothGridDispatch` 5/5; `tsc` clean for `regionMetric.ts` (461 pre-existing repo error lines untouched); `eslint --max-warnings=0` clean. Reachable ONLY under `__pfRegionLayer` (`buildMetricOuterWall` throws otherwise) and a STRICT no-op when `doRimPin` is false ⇒ production byte-identical.

**RECOMMENDATION.** (a) **Retire the "GeoStar nonMan 3 = seam-weld defect" claim** — the emitter is watertight by index (raw nonMan 0, boundary exactly 2·nRing); the 3 are `auditNonManByIndex` merging 7e-5mm-apart vertex pairs at its 1e-4mm quantize. The genuine underlying defect is **near-coincident vertices / zero-area slivers (minAngle 0.000°)** from the kernel (grid-rounding dedup `keyOf` misses points ~2e-7 apart that straddle a 1e-6 cell boundary, plus smoothing collisions) — fix at the SOURCE (robust neighbourhood dedup / fold-averse smoothing), NEVER by post-hoc welding (measured harmful). (b) **KEEP the seam-lock fix** (shipped, flag-gated): it removes a genuine density-INVARIANT seam floor that no budget increase could ever reach. (c) **GeoStar is still NOT flip-ready at 0.01mm**: the residual 0.684 is budget-starved interior under-refinement at the 5M-vertex cap. Next experiment = a de-capped convergence sweep (maxPoints 10M/20M, memory permitting) to measure whether the interior tail is genuinely density-responsive once the seam floor is gone — the prior 1.167→0.697 scaling was contaminated by the (now-removed) seam lock and must be re-derived before any "needs N tris" claim.

**LEDGER.** src fix `potfoundry-web/src/renderers/webgpu/parametric/conforming/tierC/regionMetric.ts` (`onSameRimLine`/`onSameSeamLine`/`addSplitPoint`); probe `research/bridge/_gsSeamWeld.test.ts` (PF_GSSEAM_REPRO/CTRL/PROD/DUMP/ANALYZE/DIAG/TESTFIX/WORST — env-gated, ndjson-checkpointed, resumable) + `vitest.gsseam.config.ts`. Evidence (git-ignored): `research/exchange/_gsSeamWeld/witness.ndjson` (8 rows) + `run.log` + `flat_{ut,idx}` dump. Rulers: `perFaceTrue3DSag` (true-3D, honest on GeoStar), `auditNonManByIndex` + `nonManRawBigStats` (labkit), `measureProjectorMax` (available behind PF_GSSEAM_FULL; NOT run on the final arm — the 6M-tri run exceeded 16min, so the cheaper true-3D ruler carried the verdict; the two agree on GeoStar). Commit: `5a76eb11`.

## E-2026-07-23-SMOOTHGRID-DENSITY-GUARANTEE (make `deriveSmoothGridDensity` GUARANTEE ≤tol closure by MEASURING the worst flat-facet chord and bumping the deficient axis — the FIX for the PRODCARD 3/6 GAP) [BUILD+PROVE; src edit `smoothGrid.ts`, flag-gated default-OFF byte-identical; env-gated proof PF_SMOOTHFIX]

**HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable):** appending a bounded verify-and-bump to `deriveSmoothGridDensity` — MEASURE the emitted grid's TRUE worst flat-triangle chord (`worstSmoothFacetChord`; two-stage golden-sheared top-K LOCATE + dense per-quad REFINE against the actual mesh triangle plane) and DOUBLE the deficient axis (`maxSag/n²`) ≤6× until ≤tol — closes all 7 relief-carrying smooth styles to `measureProjectorMax` MAX ≤0.01mm at prod dims (H120/Rb45/Rt70/expn1.1, registry-default opts, tol0.01), WITHOUT over-bumping the 3 already-closing styles, in <2s/derive.

**KILL-CRITERION (pre-registered):** GO iff, building each style with the SHIPPED `buildSmoothGridWall` at the NEW derived (nU,nT): (a) HR/SR/WI/HexHive `measureProjectorMax` (nTheta2048/nZ1024) MAX ≤0.01 (were 0.0115–0.0183); (b) SFB/SE/FB still ≤0.01 AND nU/nT UNCHANGED from seed (no over-bump); (c) all watertight-by-index (nonMan0, boundary=2·nU); (d) deriveSmoothGridDensity <2s/call; (e) `worstSmoothFacetChord` AGREES with `measureProjectorMax` within ~10% (else densify — do not ship a metric that disagrees).

**VERDICT: CONFIRMED — 7/7 close ≤0.01 MAX, 0 over-bump, all watertight, all derive <1.6s, metric agrees 1.00–1.04×.** All KILL-CRITERION legs met.

**MECHANISM DISCOVERY — the gap is nT-deficiency (coarse VERTICAL rows), NOT the nU-azimuthal-undershoot the PRODCARD assumed.** The seed sizes nU generously (pow2 snap ≥ nURaw) but nT only to `ceil(nTRaw)` (HR 104, SR 193, WI 231, HexHive 335) — 7–11× coarser vertical spacing than azimuthal. The measured deficient-axis test (`maxSagT/nT² ≥ maxSagU/nU²`) correctly doubles nT: HR/WI/SR each close on ONE nT-doubling (→208/462/386, nU UNCHANGED); HexHive needs both (2048/335→2048/670→4096/670 — its fine hex relief is genuinely 2D). **That doubling nT reduces HR 0.01225→0.00690 PROVES nT was the reducible axis** (a pure-nU gap is nT-invariant) — refuting the PRODCARD's "azimuthal crest" attribution as a visual-crest misread (the chord was t-bridged). Doubling nT preserves the pow2 COLUMN lattice ⇒ exact-dyadic judge cert intact.

**Two `worstSmoothFacetChord` mis-measurements found + fixed during the build (the task's sanctioned "densify until agree"):** (1) STAGE-1 ALIASING — a fixed 1024-u LOCATE grid shares a factor with pow2 nU ⇒ every sample lands at fu≡0 (column boundary, chord≈0) ⇒ BLIND to the intra-column crest that IS the gap; fixed by a golden-ratio per-row u-shear. (2) SINGLE-ARGMAX UNDER-READ (~7% on SR/HexHive) — at bumped density the true worst facet sits on a SECONDARY crest outside the argmax's ±4 window; fixed by refining the TOP-K (32) locate candidates. Post-fix agreement went 0.94→1.00× (SR), 0.96→1.01× (HexHive). Perf held <2s by a 640×512 locate (top-K supplies the accuracy, not resolution) + a precompute↔on-the-fly crossover cap.

**EVIDENCE (real vitest node-env, `%TEMP%/pf_smoothfix.ndjson`; ruler = `measureProjectorMax` true-3D perpendicular nTheta2048/nZ1024; before = registry PRODCARD except HexHive self-measured at its seed 2048/335):**

**VERDICT: 3/6 CLOSED, 3/6 GAP — GAPs small, chord-driven, and RULER-ROBUST (density undershoot, not a representation failure).** CLOSED: SuperformulaBlossom 0.00595, SuperellipseMorph 0.00796, FourierBloom 0.00631. GAP: HarmonicRipple 0.01225, SpiralRidges 0.01667, WaveInterference 0.01825. **MECHANISM of the GAPs — sag-heuristic density UNDERSHOOT at the worst azimuthal crest facet (density-responsive, NOT representation):** `deriveSmoothGridDensity` estimates the worst chord sag from a COARSE 128² probe grid and applies safety×1.5, then rounds `nU` UP to pow2. ## E-2026-07-23-DS-TIPCONE-RULER (is the DragonScales scale-tip "~0.096mm cone-apex concession" a REAL density-invariant floor, a RULER artifact, or a fan-off/under-resolution reading?) [audit-first; probe-only, env-gated PF_DSTIP_*; NO src edit; NOT committed at pre-reg]

**HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable):** the DragonScales scale-tip "cone-apex concession" (~0.096mm MAX, alleged density-invariant floor) is REFUTED at production density. The production cone-fan wall (`buildDsConeFanWallGeometric`, `__pfDsConeFan`, DS-SLIVER defaults, nU4096) has a TRUE-3D PERPENDICULAR chord at the scale-tip apex ≤0.01mm, and that apex MAX is density-RESPONSIVE (~C/√tris), NOT a floor. The 0.096 is NOT a 1/cos radial artifact of `measureProjectorMax` (that ruler is `buildRadialSurfaceProjector` = a globally-correct PERPENDICULAR projector, NOT a same-θ radial ruler) — it is the reading of an UNDER-RESOLVED / FAN-OFF mesh (the plain ring-strip / region kernel floor the apex at ~0.04–0.10; the cone-fan closes it).

**KILL-CRITERION (pre-registered):** concession REFUTED iff, at production density (nU4096, DS-SLIVER defaults, BOTH DEFAULT_DIMENSIONS Rt70/Rb45/expn1.1 AND registry Rt50/Rb40): (a) fan-face apex true-3D MAX ≤0.01mm by ALL THREE of `perFaceTrue3DSag` (re-lifted), `buildRadialSurfaceProjector` on the EMITTED f32 verts (the measureProjectorMax engine, incl. placement channel), and `bruteNearestOnRadialSurface` on the worst apex faces; AND (b) the nU sweep {1024,2048,4096,8192} shows the apex MAX shrinking ≥1.4× per nU-doubling (∝1/√tris), NOT floored; AND (c) the globally-correct perpendicular projector does NOT read ~0.096 on the cone-fan apex (agrees with perFaceTrue3DSag ≤0.01). Concession CONFIRMED (real floor) iff apex true-3D MAX floors >0.01 across the sweep under the brute gold-standard AND a specific geometric mechanism (misplaced apex / degenerate fan face / non-cone junction) is identified.

**DISCRIMINATOR (cheapest):** ONE build of the SRC production cone-fan + FOUR rulers on the SAME fan faces (perFaceTrue3DSag re-lifted; buildRadialSurfaceProjector on emitted verts; perFaceChordSag radial same-(u,t) for the 1/cos cross-check; brute worst-40). Provenance leg: reproduce ~0.096 by (i) measuring the FAN-OFF ring-strip apex at the same nU, and (ii) running the full `measureProjectorMax` (async) with/without tread-aware on cone-fan vs no-fan — attribute the headline to fan-off vs tread-inflation vs cone. nU sweep = the floor-vs-converge discriminator.

**VERDICT: CONCESSION REFUTED — the scale-tip cone apex is CLOSED, not a floor; ALL THREE task hypotheses fail as stated.** At production density (nU4096, DS-SLIVER defaults) the cone-fan scale-tip apex true-3D perpendicular MAX is **0.005102mm (Rt70 default dims) / 0.003672mm (Rt50 registry dims)** — FIVE independent rulers AGREE to 4 decimals (`perFaceTrue3DSag` re-lifted 0.005102, `buildRadialSurfaceProjector`/the measureProjectorMax engine on re-lifted 0.005102 AND on the EMITTED f32 verts 0.005100, `bruteNearestOnRadialSurface` full-azimuth gold-standard 0.005102, radial same-(u,t) `perFaceChordSag` 0.005103 ⇒ **radial/true = 1.00×**). Apex-vertex placement = **0.000005mm** (f32 floor — the apex sits EXACTLY on the analytic tip; 128/128 apexes placed, 0 skipped; nonMan-by-index 0, crack→2). **(1) NOT a 1/cos radial artifact:** `measureProjectorMax`'s engine is `buildRadialSurfaceProjector` = a globally-correct PERPENDICULAR projector (verified in src + by emitted-vert agreement with brute), NOT a same-θ radial ruler; on the fan the graded polar faces are so small+isotropic that radial≡perpendicular≡brute (1.00×), so there is NO cone overstatement to correct. **(2) NOT a placement/apex-centering bug:** placement 5nm, fan apex-exact. **(3) A cone IS closable by a flat-triangle fan (task's own claim CONFIRMED):** density sweep {1024→2048→4096} apex = 0.042309 → 0.012895 → **0.005102** (monotone, ~2.5–3.3× per nU-doubling — steeper than 1/√tris), and a 6-ring deep-fan @nU4096 = 0.005102 (unchanged ⇒ the apex POINT singularity is already fully resolved; the 0.005 residual is the fan-BLOCK PERIMETER chord, not the tip). Definitively DENSITY-RESPONSIVE, not floored.**

**ROOT CAUSE of the "0.096 density-invariant floor" belief — TWO conflated numbers, neither the cone-fan apex, both HONEST-ruler readings:**
- **The "~0.096" = the FAN-OFF mesh's under-resolved scale-tip cone.** With `__pfDsConeFan` OFF (the currently-SHIPPED default) the plain ring-strip apex = **0.184233mm @nU2048 (brute-confirmed: reGN=global=brute all 0.184233)**; the same-window nU4096 fan-off apex = **0.077375mm** (≈ the quoted 0.096, and ≈ the registry region-kernel base fwd 0.102, E-DS-HYBRID D1). This is a REAL mesh chord on a NO-apex-vertex mesh (the ruler is honest — radial=perp=brute), density-RESPONSIVE (fan-off ≈60/√tris), NOT invariant. The cone-fan closes it 15–36× (0.077→0.005 same window; 0.184→0.005 whole-apex).
- **The separately-quoted "0.82" (prod-export-truth audit "DS ON 0.82") = the C0 TREAD RISER single-valued-ruler artifact — NOT the cone.** Whole-mesh `perFaceTrue3DSag` MAX = **0.825186 @t=0.87499, dz-to-ring 0.0017mm (a tread at t=7/8), dtToCrest 0.062 (FAR from any apex); RING-band MAX = 0.825186, BODY(dz>1mm) MAX = 0.042309 (=the nU1024 cone apex).** The double-valued vertical tread wall cannot be represented by single-valued rA, so any single-valued ruler fabricates ~½-step inflation THERE. This is a ruler artifact on the treads (faithful vertical walls by construction; the tread-aware / Φ multi-sheet ruler reads them ≤tol), NOT a fidelity failure and NOT the cone apex. The task's intuition "a ruler inflates DS" is half-right — but it is the TREADS (0.82, single-valued-vs-C0), not the cone (0.096, which is fan-off under-resolution), and the mechanism is single-valued-vs-double-valued, NOT radial-vs-perpendicular.

## E-2026-07-22-LOWPOLY-GRID-CLOSE (does LowPolyFacet close whole-mesh true-3D MAX ≤0.01 at PRODUCTION scale on the SHIPPED smooth-grid emitter, and judge-certify?) [audit-first; probe-only, env-gated PF_LOWPOLY; NO src edit; NOT committed]

**HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable):** LowPolyFacet (ID 19, registry defaults lpFacets12/lpTiers1/lpAmp0.12/lpBevel0.15/lpJitter0.15) — the rank-1 layered-class tractability candidate (12 static VERTICAL facet edges, lpTiers=1 ⇒ no horizontal C0 step, no junctions) — closes to whole-mesh true-3D MAX ≤0.01mm at PRODUCTION scale (OD140/H120 ⇒ H120/Rt70/Rb45/expn1.1) on the shipped `buildSmoothGridWall` by DENSITY (uniform periodic grid), and judge-certifies via `certifyPeriodicGridMesh`. Certify on the **MAX** (not p99), seam + facet edges INCLUDED (the HexHive lesson).

**KILL-CRITERION (pre-registered):** GO iff a smooth-grid rung hits whole-mesh true-3D MAX ≤0.01 (dense per-facet, seam + rim included) + judge ACCEPT under the 1.05M-tri cap. NO-GO iff the whole-mesh MAX floors >0.01 with no tractable density/alignment lever. Split: pow2-by-density vs facet-aligned nU (mult of 12); if facet-aligned closes at far fewer tris ⇒ the sharp edges are an ALIGNMENT problem, not a density one.

**DISCRIMINATOR (cheapest):** char the surface FIRST — periodicity |rA(0⁺)−rA(2π⁻)| + 12-facet tiling |rA(θ)−rA(θ+2π/12)|; edge anatomy (is the bevel active or a SHARP C0 corner?); rim jump |rA(θ,H)−rA(θ,H⁻)|. Then a true-3D `perFaceTrue3DSag` (preFilter 0.001) nU-ladder split **whole-mesh vs rim-excluded body**: pow2 {256..8192}×nT128 (afford nU8192 under 3M since vertical sag is negligible) vs facet-aligned mult-24 {48,240,504,1008} vs control mult-12-not-24 {252}. Brute-cross-check the worst pow2 edge facets (`bruteNearestOnRadialSurface`, GN overstates sharp corners). Cert via `certAdapter.certifyPeriodicGridMesh`. Watertight via `nonManRawBigStats`.

**VERDICT: NO-GO for strict whole-mesh MAX ≤0.01 on the shipped smooth grid at defaults — TWO independent blockers, both density-INVARIANT at the whole-mesh MAX (~0.72mm on EVERY rung). (A) RIM floor() bug: lpTiers=1 makes tierIdx=floor(t) jump 0→1 exactly at t=1, injecting a 1.124mm azimuthal phase step into the analytic surface at z=H (DS-rim-bug class); the emitter's top row (t=1) sits on the shifted pattern ⇒ top face-row true-3D ~0.72mm. (B) SHARP C0 convex facet edges: the task premise "bevel-rounded C1 edges k≈2.1mm" is REFUTED — the bevel is INACTIVE at defaults (k=2.1mm < 2.09mm edge prominence; needs rFace>0.97·r0 but rFace maxes at 0.911·r0), so LowPolyFacet-at-defaults is a FLAT-FACED 12-gon PRISM with sharp C0 vertical ridges (edge slope L +103 / R −103). It is PERIODIC (12 facets tile 2π exactly; seam step 1e-6, tile step 1e-14) — so NO HexHive-style irreducible seam; both blockers are FIXABLE. The facet BODY (rim excluded) closes: pow2 needs nU=8192 (2.08M tris) — 1/nU chord law 0.175→0.088→0.044→0.022→0.011→0.0055 — but facet-ALIGNED nU=mult-24 (columns land ON the edges u=odd/24) closes at TRIVIAL nU=48 (12k tris; faces are flat planes ⇒ ridge-aligned columns tessellate exactly). "Multiple of 12" is NOT enough: 252 (mult-12-not-24) is the WORST (body 0.207) — edges maximally straddle. ## E-2026-07-19-DS-CONVERGE-B-FLANK — does wiring the ANISOTROPIC (II,I) curvature metric + metric-in-circle flip into the PRODUCTION region kernel (C1 `regionMetric` `aniso` opt) close/move the DragonScales NEAR-RING FLANK residual (E-DS-RISER-CLOSE: 0.05≤|dz|<1mm max 0.343 / p99 0.321 — the isotropic-plateau class the S2 verdict named for "the anisotropic M=g/h² accelerator")? [CONVERGE-B, FLANK half; PRE-REGISTERED kill-criterion in the probe header before measuring]

**VERDICT: MOVES (strong measured PARTIAL) — anisotropy is the RIGHT lever but NOT sufficient alone; it does NOT CLOSE the flank to 0.01, and neither more budget (HD 500k→1M bit-identical) NOR the obvious `chordSteiner` fix (REFUTED, made it worse 0.102→0.318) closes it — the close needs a STRUCTURED along-flank mechanism. HONEST, BOUNDED WALL.** At EQUAL 500k-vertex budget (both ~1M tris, identical DS graph/config, ONLY variable = `aniso`): flank composite MAX **0.343→0.102 (3.4×)**, p99 **0.295→0.040 (7.4×)**, flank outliers 6000+→4084; AND — SHARED BENEFIT, unprompted — the isotropic BODY plateau BREAKS too: bodyWit p99 **0.0199→0.0112**, bodyWit MAX **0.216→0.056**, body outliers 43062→6727 (6.4×). Watertight preserved (nonMan 0 both arms). This is the FIRST measurement of the aniso (II,I) metric IN the region kernel (with its chordTolMm guard) — prior work tested it only in the guard-less `buildCreaseAlignedMesh` (STALLED 130k/0.6mm) and the ISO metric in this kernel (plateaus). The chord guard is why it does NOT stall here. BUT three costs, none disqualifying and none free: **(1) flank MAX 0.102 ≫ 0.01** — the residual RELOCATES from across-flank (ISO worst rSpan 0.6–1.0mm) to LONG-ALONG-FLANK curvature chords (ANISO worst-12 ALL at t≈0.62 near ring k5, rSpan 1.6–2.3mm): the anisotropic long-along facets now chord the flank's OWN along-length curvature — anisotropy trades the across-flank residual for an along-flank one it does not itself remove; **(2) BUILD COST 5.6×** (ISO 58s → ANISO 329s CPU) — the metric-in-circle flip (Cholesky-whiten + Euclidean inCircle per flip) is the bottleneck; **(3) SLIVERS are REAL, not merely a wrong-ruler artifact** — isotropic %<20° 1.4→47.8%, and even the anisotropic METRIC min-angle (the honest ruler for an aniso mesh — where a correct long-along-flank cell is NOT a sliver) reads **36.8%** (metric minAng 0.171°); the chord guard's across-flank splits + the metric-in-circle flip DO create genuine slivers ⇒ the msurf-memory "DS 22.7→2.3%" (measured on the guard-less `buildCreaseAlignedMesh`) does NOT reproduce in the region kernel. **HD CONFIRM (decisive — turns "budget-starved partial" into "convergence-floor WALL"):** the ANISO flank 0.102 is NOT budget-starvation — the kernel CONVERGES (added===0) at ~491k verts (981,804 tris) BELOW the 500k cap, so raising the budget 500k→1M leaves the mesh BIT-IDENTICAL (981,804 tris, flank 0.101827, same worst-facet dump). The wall is that the chord guard splits the metric-LONGEST (across-flank) edge while the residual sag is ALONG-flank ⇒ it splits the wrong axis, dedupe-rejects, and the loop halts — a mechanism fix (along-flank/Steiner split), NOT more budget.

**MECHANISM:** the isotropic region kernel sizes h₃D = √(8·tol/κ_MAX) EQUALLY in every direction, so on the near-vertical near-ring flank it must make cells fine ACROSS *and* ALONG the flank ⇒ O(1/h²) points, exhausting the budget before the chord guard closes the across-flank sag (ISO flank MAX 0.343 = budget-starved). The aniso (II,I) metric sizes each principal direction by ITS OWN |κ_i| (fine across κ_max, long along κ_min) so the SAME across-flank chord guarantee costs O(1/h) points, freeing budget ⇒ 3.4× lower flank MAX at equal budget. The metric-in-circle flip keeps the connectivity long-along/thin-across so the point layout is not flattened into cross-curvature slivers. The WALL: where the flank curves ALONG its length (near a staggered ring), the long-along facets chord that along-curvature; the metric's κ_min sizing under-resolves it (near-ring along-curvature aliases under the FD step) and the chord guard splits the metric-LONGEST (across) edge, not the along edge — so it cannot remove the relocated along-flank residual.

**DISCRIMINATOR:** the CERTIFIED V11g composite ruler (`_ds_prodtruth_lib.buildConformRuler` = radial sheet twin 2048×3072 ∪ riser-wall, z-gated — the E-DS-PERP-MAX instrument). FLANK = ring-band (centroid ≤1mm of a ring) ∩ 0.05≤|dz|<1mm, scored vs the full composite over the worst-6000-by-radial (radial ≥ sheet ≥ composite ⇒ SOUND for MAX + the PASS). BODY = perFaceTrue3DSag witness (facet→nearest radial surface; faithful off-ring). PRODUCTION `regionMetric.ts buildMetricMesh` fed PRODUCTION `buildDragonScalesConformingGraph` (θ+toe+seamRail128, NO riser — riser is the TREAD/workstream-A half and barely moves the flank), no rim-pin (matches DS-INTERIOR-CLOSE/RISER-CLOSE). Config tolMm0.01/hMin0.02/hMax8/sizeRes192/fineStep0.0022/chordTolMm0.01/chordSampleN8/guardManifoldAlways, recoverySubdivideCollinear, 500k screen. ISO reproduces the banked baseline EXACTLY (flank 0.343223 ≡ E-DS-RISER-CLOSE 0.34322) ⇒ the ruler + decomposition are faithful.

**KILL-CRITERION (pre-reg):** CLOSE iff ANISO flank composite MAX ≤0.01 AND p99 ≤0.01, nonMan 0. MOVES iff ANISO flank MAX < 0.7×ISO. NO-OP/WALL iff ≥0.9×ISO. → **MOVES FIRED** (0.102 < 0.7×0.343 = 0.240); CLOSE did NOT (0.102 ≫ 0.01).

**EVIDENCE (screen 500k pts; certified V11g composite; flank = worst-6000-by-radial, 0.05≤|dz|<1mm):**
| arm | tris | flank MAX | flank p99 | flank out | bodyWit p99 | bodyWit MAX | %<20° iso | minAng° | nonMan | build CPU |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISO | 998,172 | 0.343 | 0.295 | 6000+ | 0.0199 | 0.216 | 1.4 | 0.3 | 0 | 58s |
| ANISO | 981,804 | **0.102** | **0.040** | 4084 | **0.0112** | **0.056** | 47.8 | 0.1 | 0 | 329s (5.6×) |

**HD CONFIRM (ANISO @ 1M cap):** BIT-IDENTICAL to the 500k screen — 981,804 tris, flank MAX **0.101827**, p99 0.039712, out 4084, bodyWit p99 0.0112, nonMan 0 ⇒ the ANISO kernel converged at ~491k verts (below both caps): the 0.102 flank is a **convergence FLOOR**, budget-independent. Metric-min-angle (honest aniso ruler) **%<20° 36.8%, minAng 0.171°** (iso ruler 47.8%) ⇒ slivers are partly-but-not-only a ruler artifact. Note: ISO @500k is budget-capped (499k verts, still refining toward its ~0.33 plateau — banked RISER-CLOSE); ANISO reaches 0.102 at FEWER verts (491k) — better fidelity at fewer points, then floors.

**ANISO_STEINER (the pre-registered fix — REFUTED @ 500k):** aniso metric + metric-flip + `chordSteiner` (worst-sag interior Steiner in the chord guard instead of the metric-longest-edge split) → flank MAX **0.318** (WORSE than plain ANISO 0.102, ≈ ISO), p99 0.123, converged at even FEWER verts (**339k**, 677,307 tris), bodyWit p99 0.0116, iso %<20° 43.2 / metric 25.5, nonMan 0. WHY WORSE: the isolated Steiner locally "satisfies" one facet and the loop halts EARLIER, REPLACING the propagating longest-edge refinement FRONT that plain ANISO used to drive the across-flank density ⇒ it under-refines. The along-flank residual is NOT an isolated interior apex (like a Gothic V) that a Steiner converges — it is a distributed along-length curvature that needs a propagating split. Steiner worst facets relocate to dz≈0.1mm (nearer the ring) — the tread-adjacent flank.

**RECOMMENDATION:** KEEP C1 (`regionMetric`/`surfaceMetricField` `aniso` opt, default-off byte-identical, watertight) as a MEASURED bulk-improver banked for the DS-close programme; do NOT flip (flank MAX 0.102 ≫ 0.01; 5.6× build; slivers real 36.8%). The HD confirm makes the wall precise and NOT-budget: the convergence floor is the chord guard splitting the metric-LONGEST (across-flank) edge while the residual is ALONG-flank. **(a) `chordSteiner` — the obvious fix — was TESTED and REFUTED** (ANISO_STEINER: flank 0.102→0.318 WORSE, converges at 339k vs 491k verts): the isolated interior Steiner halts the refinement front and under-refines; the along-flank residual is a distributed along-length curvature, not an isolated apex. So the along-flank close needs a lever that does NOT exist yet: force a split of the ALONG-flank edge specifically (the metric-longest is across; a directional guard would need the SHORT metric edge), OR emit the near-ring flank as a STRUCTURED strip (rows along the flank, columns marching across — the same structured-emission answer RISER-CLOSE reached for the tread), rather than free-Delaunay refinement. **(b) a CHEAPER flip** (the metric-in-circle Cholesky is the 5.6× cost) — A/B aniso-metric + default iso flip to attribute how much of the 3.4× is METRIC vs FLIP (if the metric alone carries most of it, drop the expensive flip, take the sliver hit under a post-pass collapse). **(c)** the real slivers (metric 36.8%) need the edge-collapse cleanup DS-INTERIOR-CLOSE already named. NET: the aniso accelerator DOES break the isotropic plateau (body 0.0199→0.0112, flank 3.4×/7.4× at fewer verts) — a necessary, measured piece — but it is NOT the whole DS-flank close, and the two obvious in-kernel finishers (budget, chordSteiner) are both refuted; the close needs a STRUCTURED along-flank mechanism (parallel to the tread curtain), not more free-Delaunay levers.

**LEDGER:** C1 src `tierC/surfaceMetricField.ts` (`aniso` ChordOpts + `anisoCurvatureMetric` export) + `tierC/regionMetric.ts` (`aniso` MetricMeshOpts + metric-in-circle flip) + `tierC/surfaceMetricAniso.test.ts` (byte-identical-off + mechanism unit, 5/5 green), commit **d23b8cbe**. ## E-2026-07-19-GEOSTAR-CREASE-CDT-BYCONSTRUCTION — does routing GeometricStar's chevron as a CREASES-ONLY complex through the double-valued mesher's constrained-CDT-BY-CONSTRUCTION path (cdt2d inserts each crease as a hard constraint edge; RECOVERY CANNOT FAIL) close its true-3D MAX toward 0.01mm — where the M=g/h² region kernel's POST-HOC edge RECOVERY failed (embedded only ~81% of edges; MAX regressed 0.367→1.250, watertight 0→93 nonMan; E-2026-07-19-GEOSTAR-CHEVRON-CONFORM)? The MAX **RELOCATES** from "the whole cliff" (plain) to the chevron **APEXES / V-TURNS / star-points** (render shows red blobs EXACTLY there) — sheet facets spanning the near-vertical wall AT the sharp corners, where arc-length crease sampling under-resolves the V-turn AND the two level curves pinch to a razor-thin strip. **MECHANISM CORRECTION (load-bearing):** the failure is NOT recovery (100% embed here) — it is that conforming the two cliff EDGES leaves the near-vertical WALL BETWEEN them chorded by sheet facets, and the apex corners are the irreducible tail. ## E-2026-07-13-MSURF-ISOVSSURF — does M=g/h² (surface-intrinsic first-form metric) MATERIALLY beat production ISOTROPIC scalar sizing on the two open frontiers (SLIVER quality + DS body/ring FIDELITY), for DragonScales + GeometricStar? [PRE-REGISTERED kill-criterion below, committed in the probe header before measuring]

**VERDICT: M-METRIC-ACCELERATES — on the SLIVER frontier, decisively and on BOTH styles; NEUTRAL-to-POSITIVE on fidelity (no body-fidelity regression at adequate density; the residual is the discontinuity-band needle class M cannot fix, orthogonal to the metric choice).**

**HYPOTHESIS:** meshing under M=g/h₃D² (even ON the 3D surface, `surfaceMetricField.ts` CHORD mode + gradeBeta, via gmsh BAMG) cuts slivers ≥30% relative AND holds DS body/ring true-3D fidelity vs the production-analog ISOTROPIC scalar sizing (even in the FLAT (u,t) rectangle, `buildIsotropicSizingField`, gmsh Frontal-Delaunay), at matched chord tolerance.

**DISCRIMINATOR (clean A/B, ONE oracle, same chord target):** gmsh on the SAME unit (u,t) square at the SAME tolMm; ONLY the size field differs — iso scalar h(u,t) (Frontal-Delaunay) vs M=g/h₃D² tensor (BAMG Alg 7). No kernel fork. SLIVERS = `triangleQualityDistribution` (minAngle + pctBelow20); DS FIDELITY = the validated §V11g composite ruler (`_ds_prodtruth_lib`, BODY dense-45 radial-bound [sheet=radial, exact] vs RING-band composite-BVH, split); GeoStar FIDELITY = `perFaceTrue3DSag` (fair relative true-3D). Watertight-by-position `auditNonManByIndex`=0 on all 8 (u=0/u=1 lift to same xyz).

**KILL-CRITERION (pre-registered):** ACCELERATES iff on BOTH styles, matched tolMm, tris within ~1.5×: surf pctBelow20 ≤ 0.7× iso AND surf minAngle ≥ iso AND DS surf body/ring p99 not worse than iso by >0.005mm. MARGINAL iff <30% reduction or fidelity regresses. NO-HELP iff surf pctBelow20 ≥ iso.

**EVIDENCE (8 cells; DIMS H120/Rb40/Rt50; SIZE_RES 192; gradeBeta 0.2):**

| style | tol | arm | tris | **pctBelow20** | minAng° | med° | p5° | body/true3d p50 | body/true3d p99 | ring p99 (DS) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DS | 0.02 | iso | 343625 | **21.8%** | 5.3 | 26 | 14 | 0.0187 | 0.0527 | 0.152 |
| DS | 0.02 | **surf** | 282366 | **1.8%** | 7.4 | 49 | 32 | 0.0123 | 0.109 | 0.189 |
| DS | 0.01 | iso | 643522 | **22.7%** | 5.6 | 26 | 14 | 0.0097 | 0.0291 | 0.115 |
| DS | 0.01 | **surf** | 566234 | **2.3%** | 5.1 | 49 | 33 | 0.0061 | 0.0305 | 0.141 |

| GeoStar | 0.01 | **surf** | 330268 | **5.8%** | 5.0 | 46 | 18 | 0.0006 | 0.104 | — |

**FINDINGS:**
1. **SLIVERS — M-metric wins decisively, BOTH styles, DENSITY-ROBUST.** pctBelow20: DS 22.7%→2.3% (~10×), GeoStar 18.2%→5.8% (~3×); median minAngle 26–27°→46–49°, p5 10–14°→18–33°. The iso rate is DENSITY-INVARIANT (DS 21.8%@0.02 ≈ 22.7%@0.01) — confirming the mechanism is the PARAMETRIZATION ANISOTROPY √E/√G≈2.4 of S(u,t)=(r·cosθ,r·sinθ,z): a (u,t)-equilateral cell is a ~2.4:1 sliver in 3D, invariant to refinement. M=g/h² removes exactly this by making cells 3D-square. Well past the pre-reg 30%-relative bar.
2. **BUDGET — M is FREE-to-CHEAPER on DS, +tris on GeoStar.** DS surf uses FEWER tris (0.82×/0.88×) because it stops over-refining the near-straight AXIAL direction that iso's scalar field wastes density on. GeoStar surf uses MORE (1.46×/1.92×) — its chevron κ_max pulls extra u-density — but stays within ~2×.
3. **DS BODY FIDELITY — no regression at adequate density.** At tol=0.02 surf body p99 REGRESSED (0.109 vs 0.053) — a COARSE-density artifact: M's κ_max (max principal curvature) sizing under-resolves the AXIAL relief between rings that iso's directional 2nd-difference catches. At the proper tol=0.01 the gap CLOSED (surf 0.0305 ≈ iso 0.0291, within the 0.005 clause) with FEWER body outliers (94k vs 252k). So body fidelity is neutral-to-better once density is adequate.
4. **DS RING band + GeoStar chevron — the residual is the discontinuity-needle class, NOT the metric.** DS surf ring p99 slightly worse (+0.026mm) — axial coarsening at the riser bands; ring p50 much better (0.0016 vs 0.006). GeoStar surf true-3D fidelity is BETTER on every stat (p99 0.283→0.104, over-0.01 26.6%→15.9%) but partly from +tris. Neither arm closes the ring/chevron to ≤0.01 (both need the step/chord guard). This residual is exactly the CROSS-CURVATURE crest-flank needle class E-2026-07-05-ANISO-RULER measured (M-angle ≡ iso-3D-angle there): M fixes the BULK parametrization slivers it was never contradicted on, and leaves the fidelity-forced discontinuity needles it was correctly refuted on. Fully consistent.

**RECOMMENDED WIRING (the answer to the mission):** feed the ANISOTROPIC M=g/h² tensor to the ALREADY-WIRED `curvatureFloor` hook (`AnalyticCurvatureFloor.ts`/`MetricSizingField.ts`) IN PLACE OF today's scalar isotropic curvature — this is the sliver closer (10×/3× pctBelow20 at ≤ or ~2× tris). TWO required companions, both already existing levers: (a) keep the `chordTolMm`/directional chord-sag guard ON (surf's κ_max sizing under-resolves axial relief → the body p99 needs the guard, NOT more isotropic density); (b) the RING/chevron discontinuity bands still need the step/feature guard (the residual 1.8–5.8% + ring p99 is the fidelity-forced needle class, not closable by ANY isotropic-or-anisotropic sizing — same conclusion as ANISO-RULER/RELAX). Do NOT expect M to reach the Gothic zero-width-apex case (element-level, refuted separately).

**HONEST CAVEATS:** (1) budget matched by equal tolMm not equal tris; deltas reported with both tris shown. (2) GeoStar fidelity via `perFaceTrue3DSag` (single-seed GN) may overstate absolute on the chevron but is fair as a same-ruler-both-arms RELATIVE delta. (3) both arms mesh the [0,1]² square (u-seam watertight-by-position, nonMan=0); this is the pure sizing-field isolation, not the production feature-conforming closer. (4) no dense >0.8M confirm — the mechanism (parametrization anisotropy) is density-invariant (shown by iso 0.02≈0.01), so a higher-density run cannot change the sliver verdict.

**LEDGER:** NEW `research/bridge/_msurf_isoVsSurf.test.ts` (PF_MSURF=1) + `vitest.msurf.config.ts`; scorecard `research/exchange/_msurf_isoVsSurf/scorecard.ndjson` (8 rows) + persisted `_{style}_{arm}_{tol}/out_gmsh.json` meshes. Reuses `surfaceMetricField.buildSurfaceMetricField`, `sizingField.buildIsotropicSizingField`, the gmsh oracle, `_ds_prodtruth_lib` composite ruler, labkit instruments — no re-coded machinery, no src/ edit. Re-measure the ANALYTIC path (prior "multi-day intractable" was the GRID sampler kernel) at increasing domains; derive a cost model + parallelizable fraction [PRE-REGISTERED: kill = converges at tractable tris+time single-thread ⇒ FULL-POT-FEASIBLE; converges but too slow ⇒ NEEDS-PARALLELIZATION with the quantified target; fails/intractable-even-parallel ⇒ BLOCKED]

**VERDICT: NEEDS-PARALLELIZATION.** The analytic lever converges to LITERAL 0 outliers ≤0.01mm at every domain that finished — the wall is pure COMPUTE TIME, never fidelity. Prior "multi-day intractable" (sampler kernel) is REFUTED for the analytic path: it is multi-HOUR single-thread, an order below multi-day. Probe `research/bridge/_tierc_fullpot_scaling.test.ts` (+ `vitest.tierc_fullpot_scaling.config.ts`); raw `research/exchange/tierc/fullpot_*_verdict.json` + `fullpot_scaling_costmodel.json` + `fullpot_scaling_crumbs.ndjson`. Measured this machine, single-thread, AboveNormal.

| domain | style | nθ | area | state | tris | passes | refine | tris/area | ms/tri | dense%refine | vs-analytic max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GS_CI | GeoStar | 256 | 0.0025 | CONVERGED | 5071 | 7 | 14.2s | 2.03M | 2.81 | 53% | 0.00995 / 0 out |
| GS_BAND (c) | GeoStar | 1024 | 0.02 | CONVERGED | 41428 | 9 | 201s | 2.07M | 4.86 | 54% | 0.00995 / 0 out |
| GS_BAY (b) | GeoStar | 256 | 0.125 | PARTIAL (pass5/~9, 14min) | ≥264509 | — | abort | ≥2.12M | — | 43% | 11518 out remain |
| G_CI (cited) | Gothic | 512 | 0.005 | CONVERGED | 18045 | 8 | ~344s | 3.61M | ~19.1 | ~71% | 0.00995 / 0 out |
| G_BAND (c) | Gothic | 1024 | 0.024 | PARTIAL (pass5/~9, 13min; 1 dense pass = 8.4min) | ≥66673 | — | abort | ≥2.78M | — | 53% | 5499 out remain |
| G_BAY (b) | Gothic | 512 | 0.0833 | PARTIAL (pass4/~8, still PHASE-A at 21min, 0 dense reached) | ≥135766 | — | abort | ≥1.63M | — | — | 16856 out remain |

**Cost model.** Tri-density is SCALE-INVARIANT (GeoStar 2.0–2.1M tris/unit-(u,t)-area across 3 independent domains within 4%; Gothic ~3.6M converged). ⇒ full-pot tris ≈ **GeoStar 2.1M / Gothic 3.3–3.6M**. Build-time single-thread, TILED (see hazard): **GeoStar ~1.6h (nθ256) / ~2.9h (nθ1024 production); Gothic ~18h**. MONOLITHIC HAZARD: the whole-set re-CDT every pass scales ~tris^1.35 (GeoStar CI→BAND: tris ×8.2 → CDT-remainder ×17.1) ⇒ a single 2–3M-point domain is superlinear + OOM-risky; full-pot MUST be tiled into bays/regions.

**Parallelization.** Dense per-facet scoring is only 53–54% (GeoStar) / ~65–71% (Gothic) of refine ⇒ the committed `parallelScorer` 2.94× gives Amdahl total **1.55× (GeoStar) / 1.88× (Gothic)** — INSUFFICIENT alone. Two blockers: (1) `parallelScorer.samplerGrid()` THROWS on an analytic sampler — the worker reconstructs the 512² GRID (wrong surface, chords the crests), and `refineToZeroOutliersParallel` hardcodes `radialSurfaceFromSampler`+sampler-lift ⇒ the analytic lever has NO parallel path today; must serialize (styleId,params,dims)→rebuild `buildAnalyticRadiusFn` per worker + thread analytic placement/lift in. (2) PRIMARY lever = PER-BAY/REGION parallelism: full-pot = independent bays (Gothic 12 / GeoStar 8) or finer R-REFINE regions — embarrassingly parallel, near-linear to core count, and bounds each CDT (kills the superlinear blowup). With regions ≫ cores, full-pot ≈ serial_work / cores. BAR: interactive <5min unreachable on CPU; batch <30min reachable for GeoStar (~6–8 cores + regional tiling), Gothic needs ~32+ cores or GPU-offloaded analytic scoring.

**LEDGER:** NEW `research/bridge/_tierc_fullpot_scaling.test.ts`, `vitest.tierc_fullpot_scaling.config.ts`; data `research/exchange/tierc/fullpot_{GS_CI,GS_BAND,GS_BAY,G_BAND,G_BAY}_verdict.json` + `fullpot_scaling_costmodel.json` + `fullpot_scaling_crumbs.ndjson`. **KILL CRITERIA (pre-registered).** KILL-1: point-fold pre-check shows CK-class folds ⇒ STOP MEASURED-EXCLUDE. KILL-1b: loci placement can't reach sub-0.01 vs the sampler in 2 designs ⇒ report hash-precision pathology. KILL-2: recovery <90% at tractable pickets ⇒ report. KILL-3: new off-wall population ⇒ classify. CLOSED iff Newton==0 ≤10M + watertight non-vacuous + zeroArea 0.

**RESULT — VERDICT: REFUTED (the doubled-contour EMBED is a ~10× true-3D REGRESSION vs the base mesher). Voronoi is EXCLUDE-class — the base free-adaptive tessellation already handles the C0 cell-wall network BETTER than pinned contour constraints, exactly the settled weave/braid/lattice ruling ("conforming trades slivers for a true-3D chord regression"), now DEMONSTRATED for Voronoi with an apples-to-apples control.**

**KILL-1 point-fold pre-check — NOT triggered (RAMP-embeddable, NOT a CK fold).** Voronoi's r(u,t) is single-valued so a literal occlusion fold is analytically impossible. The binary "monotone both sides" probe read multivaluedFrac 0.61 but that CONFLATES the wall NETWORK (a normal ray from one wall hits an adjacent wall/junction) with an occlusion. The DECISIVE discriminator (foldcheck2): march crest→band-edge cleanly into a cell interior; the facet chord-sag FALLS geometrically under subdivision — median 0.234→0.021 (nSub 1→8), **ratio s8/s1 = 0.0895** ⇒ RAMP (reducible), not a density-invariant fold. Slope bounded ~0.96 (not diverging). So embeddable-IN-PRINCIPLE — but "embeddable" ≠ "net improvement" (the headline finding).

**Extract — loci sampler-anchored to machine precision (KILL-1b NOT triggered).** Ridge crest extracted as the Voronoi diagram edges (cellSdf=0 = the seed-id-change/equidistance locus, via `marchSeedBoundary`; cellSdf only TOUCHES 0 so isolevels just above it FRAGMENT — the 0.02-isolevel broke into 39k tiny pieces = a 49mm off-wall artifact, replaced by the clean seed-id network). Crest maxValErr 0.0019, flat (cellSdf=0.1) maxValErr 5.9e-5 (both p99≈0, 0 verts >0.01) — machine-precision, sampler-anchored (the disp3D 3.7mm max was the §V11o junction validator artifact, p99Disp=0).

**Build — PLANARIZATION was load-bearing (the §V11z / project_cdt_planarization lesson).** The Voronoi wall network CROSSES itself densely (185k raw crossings; crest-only 67k, flat-only 117k). Un-planarized crossing constraints defeat CDT recovery → giant bridging facets = a **47mm off-wall catastrophe** (1744 facets radial-bound >10mm, worst-pt at radius ~0.075 = a facet spanning half the pot). FIX: `planarizeMM` in mm-space (u→arc, t→height), splitting every crossing into a T-junction (decimated 68k-edge set planarizes clean in ~1.2s, residual 0, +504 T-junctions). Post-planarize: residualCrossings 0, nonManIdx 0, zeroArea 0, radial max 47→1.44mm. Instrument fixes: `nonManRawBig` large-mesh-safe audit (auditNonManRaw's JS-Map overflows at >16.7M edges) + persist-mesh-before-audit.

**Newton verdict — DECISIVE apples-to-apples control (same `newtonNearest` ruler, radial-prefilter + 3000 stratified, on ALL three meshes):**
| mesh | picket/chord | tris | scaledTrueOut | trueMax | truep50 | truep90 | truep99 | offWall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **anchor (BASE, no embed)** | — (b0.008/s224) | 4.0M | **10,458** | **0.0577** | 0.0090 | 0.0143 | **0.0266** | 0 |
| doubled embed s15 | 0.15/0.004 | 5.0M | 135,348 | **0.4204** | 0.0131 | 0.042 | 0.085 | 0.0004 |
| doubled embed s10 | 0.10/0.002 | 7.0M | 101,359 | **0.4204** | 0.0132 | 0.039 | 0.080 | ~0 |

**The base mesher's own free tessellation BEATS the doubled embed ~10× on every true-3D metric** (scaledTrueOut 10,458 vs 101k-135k; p99 0.027 vs 0.08; trueMax 0.058 vs 0.42). The embed CONFINES residual on-wall (offWall ~0, watertight, zeroArea 0 — the mechanism is structurally sound, like Gyroid) but the NET true-3D is far WORSE, because: (a) the C0 cell-wall crease constraints only 94% recover (5.6% failPct DENSITY-INVARIANT — junction Lawson-recovery fails like CK's oblique crossings), (b) the frozen **trueMax 0.42042 (byte-identical s15↔s10)** is a u=1 SEAM artifact (all 14 deepest facets at uc≈0.9999 — extraction doesn't wrap the wall network across the cylinder seam) — the density-invariant CLIFF signature, and (c) the on-wall ramp bulk is only weakly density-responsive (p90 0.042→0.039 for +40% tris) and never descends below the base floor. DENSITY TRAJECTORY: scaledTrueOut 135k→101k (bulk responds) but trueMax + p90/p99 PINNED ⇒ no path to literal-0, and every operating point is a REGRESSION on the base.

**VERDICT: REFUTED / EXCLUDE-class CONFIRMED. The doubled-contour EMBED — the exact §V11u-3-recommended mechanism — makes Voronoi's true-3D WORSE, not better. Voronoi joins BasketWeave/CelticKnot/CelticTriquetra as MEASURED-EXCLUDE (the settled weave/braid/lattice map): its C0 nearest-cell-wall network is a discontinuity that the free-adaptive base mesher tessellates better than any pinned-constraint conforming embed. RECOMMENDATION: accept the §V11u-3 honest floor as the Voronoi export figure (base mesher, ~10k true-3D outliers @ p99 0.027, worst 0.058 — geometrically faithful, the designed cellular relief; radial overstates). Do NOT invest further embed/density budget — the apples-to-apples control PROVES the embed regresses. Distinct from Gyroid (whose SMOOTH TPMS wall embedded to literal-0 §V11aa): Voronoi's walls are a DISCONTINUOUS min-of-distances network (C0 creases + junctions + a periodic seam), not a smooth level set — the embed's constraint-recovery + seam-wrap failures dominate. This RESOLVES the last doubled-contour-EMBED candidate from the §V11u-3 fork.**

## E-2026-07-08-TIERC-TAPERRAIL — the LAST unrun Gothic flank-band lever: rail af-levels placed at equal cumulative STEEPNESS (|∇r|) intervals instead of fixed af values (finer rails exactly where the flank is steepest). Scoped completeness probe following §V11v LADDER-4 [PRE-REGISTERED — kill-criteria committed BEFORE measuring]

**FRAME (small scoped probe, one mechanism variant, ≤2 gate runs).** ESTABLISHED (§V11v, not re-derived): the UNIFORM LADDER-4 af{0.03,0.08,0.18,0.40} = best Gothic config (worst **0.117**, ~138-147 outliers, **~5.0M**, p99 0.00907); LADDER-5 adds cost without cutting the worst ⇒ the 0.117 is rail-count-INDEPENDENT under UNIFORM rail spacing.

**HYPOTHESIS (pre-registered).** Rail spacing tapered by local steepness (|∇r| — finer rails exactly where the flank is steepest, coarser where it eases) concentrates the framing where the 0.117-class facets live and drops the worst BELOW 0.117 at matched budget. The §V11v agent PREDICTED this floors too (under taper the widest un-framed strip is where the flank is GENTLEST, so the residual descends there — worst stays ~0.117 if right, drops if wrong).

**DISCRIMINATOR (cheapest first).** `taperedLevels()` in flankBand.ts places nRails af-levels at equal cumulative-|∇r| intervals: S(af)=∫|∇r|(af')·daf', rails at S⁻¹(k/(nRails+1)·S_total). New `taper` mode in `_flankBand.test.ts` (PF_FB=taper, PF_FB_NRAILS). ONE gate at matched budget vs LADDER-4; ceiling run only if promising.

**KILL-CRITERION (pre-registered).** GENUINE WIN = worst meaningfully BELOW 0.117 at matched budget (~5.0M). FLOOR-CONFIRMED (worst ~0.117, no gain) = equally valuable, completes the Gothic mechanism table. REGRESS (worst↑ / nonMan↑) ⇒ drop, note. Implementation >a few hours or destabilizes recovery/crossings ⇒ report why + stop.

**RESULT (FLOOR-CONFIRMED + the taper REGRESSES — the win-hypothesis is KILLED; the Gothic flank-band mechanism table is now COMPLETE).**

**MECHANISM (built, flag-gated default-OFF, byte-identical off — commit 6bbb580).** `taperedLevels(sampler,domain,nRails,afLo,afHi)`: steepness = |∇r| (radius gradient in mm PER mm of (u,t) footprint), integrated against **daf** (NOT the mm footprint — af≡(r−panel)/(crest−panel) makes r linear in af so ∫|dr| is trivially uniform; ∫|∇r|·daf crowds rails where the radius-per-parameter gradient is high = the steep shoulder). TDD unit guard `taperRail.test.ts` (analytic sqrt-skew flank ⇒ rails crowd at low af [0.035,0.066,0.125,0.237]; flat flank ⇒ uniform fallback; 3/3). Fast tierC suite GREEN (flagOff.byteIdentical + morseComplex + anisoSplit + dirtyCache + taperRail = 9/9). flankBand.ts imported ONLY by tierC tests ⇒ production byte-identical off by construction.

**TAPER EXTRACTION (the decisive intermediate finding).** On the REAL Gothic flank, taperedLevels(nRails=4) → **af[0.186, 0.259, 0.323, 0.380]** — ALL four rails CROWDED at the mid-to-upper flank; NOT ONE rail below af 0.186. Placement sub-0.01 TRUE (dispP90 0, dispMax ≤0.0096). Mechanistic why: the Gothic flank's |∇r| is HIGHEST at the mid-flank (af 0.19-0.38) and gentlest at the low toe — the steepness-taper starves the low toe of rails, exactly where LADDER-4's two low rails {0.03,0.08} lived.

**GATE (matched budget, §V11s p1 config + tapered-4 band, ×42 full-pot):**

| config | worst mm | outliers | p99 | proj | nonMan (cracked) | recovery/crossings |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LADDER-4 (uniform, §V11v best) | **0.1170** | 138-147 | 0.00907 | **5.0M** | 2 (5) | 100 / 0 |
| TAPER-4 (steepness) | **0.39553** | 184 | 0.00870 | 7.19M | 2 (5) | 100 / 0 |

The tapered variant REGRESSES on every axis — worst 0.396 vs 0.117 (**3.4× WORSE**), tris 7.19M vs 5.0M, outliers 184 vs ~140. The worst-facet ampFrac histogram is CONCLUSIVE: **178 of 184 outliers sit at af[0,0.15]** (85+69+24) — the low toe the taper left completely unframed. The frozen worst 0.39553 equals §V11v's DOUBLED-band worst (0.3955): with no rails below af 0.186 the residual reverts to the un-framed low-flank/toe strip. **The §V11v prediction is CONFIRMED EXACTLY** — the gentlest strip is the low toe, and the residual descended precisely there.

**VERDICT: FLOOR-CONFIRMED (win-hypothesis KILLED; taper REGRESSES).** worst-below-0.117 did NOT fire; uniform LADDER-4 remains the best Gothic config. The chord-sag floor lives at the LOW toe (af<0.15, panel-meets-flank) where |∇r| is LOW — so a steepness-taper places rails in exactly the WRONG band; uniform low rails are load-bearing. **The Gothic flank-band mechanism table is COMPLETE:** DOUBLED (0.396) → uniform LADDER-4 (0.117, plateau) → LADDER-5 (0.117, +cost) → NO-PICKET (0.117) → TAPER-4 (0.396, regresses). No rail-placement family beats uniform LADDER-4's 0.117; the residual is the irreducible near-vertical rib-flank chord floor > the ≤10M cap. Best-measured Gothic frontier stands at **LADDER-4: worst 0.117 / ~140 outliers / p99 0.00907 (<tol) / ~5.0M**.

**RECOMMENDATION:** accept the LADDER-4 ~5.0M / worst 0.117 / p99<tol frontier as the Gothic close (mechanism table exhausted — no rail-placement lever remains) OR raise budget ≫10M for literal-0. No further flank-band rail experiment is warranted.

**LEDGER:** spec §V11y; ceiling run NOT launched (matched-budget REGRESSED ⇒ ceiling cannot rescue a lever that starves the residual band). `flankBand.ts`+`taperedLevels`, `taperRail.test.ts`, `taper` mode in `_flankBand.test.ts`. Embed the rib-flank TOE contours (where the steep flank meets the smooth panel) as DOUBLED fine-picket constraints so each near-vertical flank is a FRAMED strip and facets end AT the flank boundaries — the PROVEN Gyroid doubled-contour close, applied to Gothic [PRE-REGISTERED — kill-criteria committed BEFORE measuring]

The needle-forbidding pickets LOWER the frontier (worst 1.06→0.47, outliers 2794→1150, proj 7.0→6.76M) but do not open the gate. ## E-2026-07-08-TIERC-ANISO-RED — ANISOTROPIC / flank-aware RED split (bisect ONLY the sag-dominant edge of an outlier rib-flank facet ⇒ ~half the tri growth of isotropic 1→4) on the multi-bay Gothic gate; converge to whole-mesh 0 UNDER 6M full-pot projection [PRE-REGISTERED — kill-criteria committed BEFORE measuring]

**FRAME (ROUND 6, follow-up to E-2026-07-08-TIERC-COSTGAP / spec §V11k → §V11m).** ESTABLISHED (not re-derived): the multi-bay Gothic gate (u[0.05,0.15]×t[0.38,0.62], tol 0.01) EXPLODES past 6M under BOTH the production isotropic-RED kernel (V11k: 144k tris @ pass-5 = 6.06M, 8306 outliers, worst bounced to 1.056) AND the research M-square kernel (V11m: outliers 2288→8196 pass-1→2, same monotone explosion). Root cause is DOMAIN, not mechanism: the full-relief arch body t[0.38,0.62] has ampMean 1.217mm (2.25× the V3 shallow-tip band's 0.541mm) ⇒ genuinely ~5.4× more expensive at tol 0.01. Seed strategy CANNOT help (V11k rib-aware REFUTED — the outliers are genuine rib-FLANK facets exceeding tol, re-inserted by the refine loop regardless of seed). The ONE untested mechanism (V11k+V11m standing recommendation): a DOWNSTREAM refine-loop lever — anisotropic RED. SLIVER-GEOMETRY FACT (spec VALIDATION 5): rib-flank needles are CROSS-CURVATURE elongated, median longest-edge angle to crest ~76°, i.e. the chord-sag direction is PERPENDICULAR to the crest. Isotropic RED 1→4 quadruples tris per outlier; splitting ONLY along the sag direction (bisect the facet's single worst-sag / longest cross-curvature edge — a 1→2 point insertion since the loop re-CDTs the whole point set each pass, so no T-junctions) buys the same sag reduction at ~half the tri growth.

**HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable):** An anisotropic split mode — insert ONLY the midpoint of the sag-dominant edge of each outlier facet (vs all 3 midpoints in isotropic RED 1→4) — reaches the SAME outlier trajectory at ≥1.3× fewer tris per pass, bringing the multi-bay Gothic gate under 6M full-pot at literal whole-mesh 0.

**DIRECTION SELECTION (2 designs, pick by measurement not aesthetics):**
- (D1 MAX-EDGE-SAG) For each outlier facet, compute the P1 midpoint chord-sag of each of its 3 edges against the surface (3 cheap surface evals); bisect ONLY the max-sag edge. The sag-dominant edge IS the across-crest / high-|r''| axis by construction.
- (D2 LONGEST-EDGE) Bisect the facet's longest CHART edge (mm-scaled) — VALIDATION 5 says the longest edge sits ~76° to the crest = across the flank = the sag direction. Cheapest (no surface eval); a pure geometry signal.
- FALLBACK: a facet whose top-2 edge signals are within a tolerance (aspect≈1 / ambiguous) falls back to isotropic RED (all 3 midpoints) — anisotropic-only could stall convergence.

**IMPLEMENTATION:** opt-in `RefineOptions.splitMode: 'aniso'` (+ `anisoDirection: 'edgeSag'|'longEdge'`, `anisoAspectTol`), default undefined ⇒ isotropic RED ⇒ BYTE-IDENTICAL to current behaviour (regression test asserts identical uv/tris hash off-flag). Constraint-respecting: a locked (constraint) edge selected as the split edge subdivides the CONSTRAINT (same [a,b]→[a,m],[m,b] rule as isotropic); midpoints on crest edges stay locked. Guard: reject a split producing a sub-DEDUPE_CELL_MM (0.004mm) edge; keep zeroArea 0.

**KILL CRITERIA (committed BEFORE measuring):**
- **CONVERGED-UNDER-6M (ACCEPTANCE) iff:** the aniso gate reaches literal whole-mesh 0 (honest dense guard, every-facet) AND watertight non-vacuous (inject-crack moves nonMan count) AND capped==false AND projFullPot < 6,000,000. ⇒ THEN GeoStar patch gate, then launch rebaseline20 detached.
- **KILL (2-DESIGN) iff:** BOTH direction-selection designs (D1, D2) fail to beat isotropic growth-per-sag meaningfully — i.e. < 1.3× tri savings at an EQUAL outlier trajectory (matched pass-by-pass outlier counts within ~15%) — OR the gate converges only ABOVE 6M. ⇒ STOP and produce the FINAL DECISION ARTIFACT: the consolidated fidelity-vs-budget frontier (outliers/max vs projected full-pot tris) for isotropic (V11k) vs aniso vs the research kernel (V11m), stated plainly for a user budget decision, PLUS the extrapolated budget that WOULD suffice for literal 0 (error bars stated).

**METHOD:** DEV-ONLY flag-gated tierC (`noBridgeRefine.ts` aniso opt-in branch in `applyScoredPass` + the sync loop; default-off byte-identical). Fast guard test `anisoSplit.test.ts` (byte-identical-off + mechanism: aniso inserts fewer pts/outlier). Head-to-head gate `_anisoGate.test.ts` (PF_TIERC_ANISOGATE=1, parallel scorer 4-worker + dirty cache, per-pass ndjson checkpoint the INSTANT computed → `research/exchange/_tierc_aniso/`). Baseline trajectory reused from disk (`_tierc_ribaware/baseline_leverA_tOnly_frontier.json`; configs match: adaptiveSeed hMin0.09 t-only, bgArcMm 0.3, tol 0.01, thetaWindow 0.5). gitnexus impact before editing existing symbols; detect_changes before commit; NEVER git add -A. NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192; ≤4 workers; explicit staging. Do NOT touch _tangled_cont/_gyroid_truth (other agents). Ledger §V11n + this row.

**VERDICT: KILL CRITERION MET (converges only ABOVE 6M) — the anisotropic split is a strictly BETTER refine mechanism but does NOT open the gate; the full-relief Gothic wall STANDS. DECISION ARTIFACT produced.**

MECHANISM CONFIRMED (the lever works): pass-1 outlier population BIT-IDENTICAL across iso/aniso (5709, worst 1.0522062713658533) ⇒ aniso targets the same outliers but inserts FEWER pts/outlier. Fast-guard: **edgeSag 1.30 inserts/outlier vs iso 2.01 (1.52× tri savings), longEdge 0.70 (2.18×), zeroArea 0**. Full gate first-dense pass (5): **edgeSag 122660 tris (5.15M) / 7142 outliers / worst 0.726 vs iso 144369 (6.06M) / 8306 / 1.056 = 1.18× fewer tris AND better fidelity**. edgeSag beats the 1.3× bar. longEdge under-performs (tracks iso: 8562 outliers / worst 1.056 — the longest CHART edge is NOT the sag axis under the t-only anisotropic seed; edgeSag is the correct direction signal).

NON-CONVERGENCE (the wall): BOTH designs PLATEAU, they do not reach 0. worst PINNED at **1.05918988549241mm** — the EXACT V11h/V11k re-forming CDT t-needle — for 5 consecutive dense passes (edgeSag p9-13; longEdge p7-8). edgeSag plateaus ~2794 outliers @ proj ~7.0M (tris grow only ~340/pass from 161k — saturated); longEdge capped, final honest guard **2251 outliers / max 1.01889 / p99 0.019 / proj 7.84M / nonMan 0 non-vacuous (crack→3)**. The V3 "1.05M converged" was the EASIER shallow-tip band (t[0.70,0.80], ampMean 0.541mm), not this full-relief body (ampMean 1.217mm).

RECOMMENDATION (per user standard — NO per-region tol accept-band): (1) BANK the anisotropic split (flag-gated, default-off byte-identical, edgeSag the correct signal) — it re-prices the wall ~1.18-1.5× cheaper per pass for any future budget-raise but does not open the gate alone; (2) the ONE remaining un-falsified direction is a SEED/TOPOLOGY lever that FORBIDS the re-forming needle (a locked short t-edge across the apex bump, or a LOCAL Bowyer-Watson insertion that does not re-CDT the whole domain — breaking the re-formation mechanism V11h identified), NOT another refine-split isotropy. **FRAME (ROUND 4, follow-up to E-2026-07-08-TIERC-ADAPTIVE-SEED / spec §V11h).** ESTABLISHED (not re-derived): the 1.05919mm pin = a re-forming long t-spanning CDT needle from a seed dead-zone (uniform bgArcMm leaves no interior points in the t≈0.38-0.48 arch-arc t-band). LEVER A's 2D sag-driven seed BREAKS the pin (worst monotone 1.05→0.73, outliers 6399→2350 dropping) but projects **8.3M full-pot** (over 6M) because the sag field fires ~uniformly (≈86,000 pts/unit-t across ALL t-bands): **RIB curvature dominates the sag field everywhere, yet ribs are ALREADY handled by the locked protected-complex constraint chains + the refine loop** — so the seed pays for rib density twice. Coarser seeds (A2) re-form the pin exactly at 1.05918988549241. This is a fidelity-vs-budget frontier IF the sag field cannot be made rib-selective; the RIB-AWARE lever tests whether it can.

**LEVER (falsifiable):** a RIB-AWARE seed field — EXCLUDE constraint-chain-carried curvature from the sag field so seeding densifies ONLY the smooth residual (the horizontal arch arc). Candidate designs (measure cheapest first):
- **(a) chain-distance MASK** — skip sag-driven cell-splitting within a chart-distance band of any protected-complex constraint chain point (the chains are dense ≤0.15mm polylines; a distance query over chain points is cheap). Rib flanks lie within the band ⇒ their sag is ignored; the smooth dead-zone bump is >band from any chain ⇒ still seeds. Cheapest, tried first.
- **(c) θ-averaged residual sag** — split cells on the sag of the θ-averaged profile r̄(t) (average r over the domain u-range at each t) instead of max-over-u. r̄(t) captures the horizontal arch arc EXACTLY and is immune to rib content (ribs average out along θ). Well-matched to the known dead-zone geometry. Tried if (a) fails.
- **(b) rib-subtracted surface proxy** — low-pass r(θ,z) along θ at rib wavelength; riskier, only if (a)+(c) both fail.

**KILL CRITERIA (committed BEFORE measuring):**
- **CONFIRM (GATE) iff** the multi-bay Gothic gate (u[0.05,0.15]×t[0.38,0.62], parallel scorer 4-worker + dirty cache ON) reaches guardOutliers==0 (honest whole-mesh dense guard, EVERY facet) AND capped==false AND watertight nonMan==0 non-vacuous (inject-crack moves the count) AND full-pot tri PROJECTION < 6M (report the projection number explicitly). AND byte-identical-off HOLDS (flagOff.byteIdentical GREEN — the rib-aware field is opt-in, default-off).
- **KILL/STOP iff** 2 rib-aware seed-field designs fail to SIMULTANEOUSLY break the pin (worst < prior plateau, outliers converging) AND stay under 6M ⇒ STOP and report the measured fidelity-vs-budget frontier (outliers/max vs projected-tris curve per design) as the honest deliverable; the user decides budget-raise vs concession. Do NOT grind a 3rd+ design past the 2-design budget.
- **T5 (GeoStar patch gate + rebaseline20) — GATED on GATE convergence** (launch detached with per-style ndjson checkpoints + honest multi-hour timeout only if the gate converges; may outlive the session — report checkpoint paths).

**VERDICT (2026-07-08) — REFUTED (both rib-aware designs track the baseline explosion; the budget wall is a REFINE-LOOP floor, not a seed floor).**

- **CHEAP DISCRIMINATOR (seed-level, `_ribAwareDiag`, PF_TIERC_RIBAWARE) — rib-aware masking BARELY changes the seed.** All designs land ~21-25k seed pts; the **dead-zone t-band [0.44,0.49] seed count is IDENTICAL** across designs (~3845 tOnly/mask, 3780 thetaAvg). The seed projects only **~1.8-2.1M full-pot** — so the ROUND-3 8.3M did NOT come from the seed; it comes from the **REFINE LOOP** RED-1→4 growth. This immediately predicted the gate result: a seed-only lever cannot change a budget consumed downstream.
- **GATE HEAD-TO-HEAD (`_ribAwareGate`, PF_TIERC_RIBGATE, parallel-scorer 4-worker + per-pass ndjson) — all three trajectories are IDENTICAL within noise.** At pass 3 (7-pt driver): baseline `leverA_tOnly` **tris 91018 / outliers 5950 / worst 0.7938**; design (c) `thetaAvg` **90236 / 6373 / 0.7938**; design (a) `mask b1.0` **91378 / 6181 / 0.7938**. The `worstMm` is BIT-IDENTICAL (0.793785701601064) across all three — the arch-arc needle is a shared geometric feature the seed does not move. Baseline's first DENSE pass (5) = **144369 tris = 6.06M full-pot, 8306 outliers, worst bounced to 1.056** ⇒ OVER 6M with thousands remaining (same A1 explosion). Also proves **uSplit on/off makes NO difference** (t-only baseline ≈ A1's u-split-ON trajectory — the un-run ROUND-3 data point, now filled).
- **ROOT CAUSE (why rib-awareness cannot help):** the outliers driving RED tri-growth are **genuine rib-FLANK facets** whose P1 chord-sag exceeds tol=0.01mm on the relief-dense Gothic wall — NOT seed artifacts. The protected complex locks the ridge LINES but the flank SURFACE between chains must still be refined to tol. Rib-aware seeding removes rib sag-splits from the SEED (2-4% fewer pts) but the refine loop RE-inserts them because the flanks genuinely exceed tol. The budget floor is the honest cost of resolving every Gothic rib flank to 0.01mm, **independent of seed strategy.**

**VERDICT SUMMARY: KILL criterion MET — 2 rib-aware seed-field designs (mask + thetaAvg) both fail to break the budget; each tracks the baseline 8M+ explosion bit-for-bit at the worst facet. The multi-bay Gothic gate does NOT converge to literal 0 under 6M by ANY seed strategy. This is a REFINE-LOOP / true-geometry fidelity-vs-budget frontier (every rib flank > tol at 0.01mm), NOT a seed dead-zone. GATE not converged ⇒ T5 (GeoStar + rebaseline20) NOT launched (gated on convergence).**

**RECOMMENDATION:** The lever must move DOWNSTREAM of the seed (the refine loop), not the seed. Two genuinely-different future directions: (1) an **anisotropic / flank-aware RED** that splits a rib-flank facet along its short axis only (halves tri growth vs isotropic 1→4) — or a curvature-aligned metric split; (2) accept the multi-bay Gothic wall as a **documented density-vs-budget concession at tol=0.01mm** and either raise the budget for feature-dense styles or relax tol on rib flanks specifically (the flanks are smooth, printer-resolvable relief — a per-region tol, not a global one). The rib-aware seed machinery (`ribAwareMode` 'mask'/'thetaAvg' + `ribBandMm`) is banked, flag-gated, byte-identical-off, in case a future refine-side lever wants a rib-selective seed to compose with.

**GUARANTEES:** only flag-gated Tier-C touched (noBridgeRefine.ts rib-aware opt-in branch + dev-only PF_TIERC_RIBAWARE/PF_TIERC_RIBGATE probes). ## E-2026-07-08-TIERC-PERF-SEAM — parallelize the whole-mesh brute scorer (worker pool, byte-identical metrology) + cross-pass dirty-facet cache + resolve the pinned seam∩domain-boundary facet, then re-run the multi-bay Gothic gate to convergence [PRE-REGISTERED — kill-criteria committed BEFORE measuring]

**FRAME (follow-up to E-2026-07-08-TIERC-JUNCTION / spec V11d):** the multi-bay Gothic plateau is NOT a junction wall — it is (d) DENSITY (a smooth low-κ ~1.5mm horizontal arch arc at t≈0.465, no ridge to detect; bgArcMm 0.3 closes the seam-free focused domain to literal 0, guardMax 0.00996) stacked on ONE pinned facet at u=0 (periodic seam ∩ domain uLo boundary, 1.0592mm, RED-1→4 cannot reduce).
