## E-2026-07-10-ASSEMBLEWATERTIGHT-SUBTIMING — sub-instrument the `assembleWatertight` bucket (94–99% of export time, per E-2026-07-09-EXPORT-STAGE-TIMING) into binary search / final quadtree rebuild / triangulation [MEASURED — instrumentation only, no optimization]

**FRAME.** Direct follow-up (user-directed) to E-2026-07-09-EXPORT-STAGE-TIMING, which found `assembleWatertight` dominating the conforming generate path (94.1–98.8% of total, 97.4% aggregate) but stopped there — that arm was explicitly scoped to the 7 top-level buckets and named its own next step: *"sub-instrument `assembleWatertight` itself — around `searchBudgetScale`'s probe iterations vs. the final kept build vs. the per-cell CDT."* This arm does exactly that.

**METHOD.** Reading `ConformingWall.ts` end to end (not inferring from the doc comments — see FINDING 3 below) shows `buildConformingWall`'s two-step structure per wall: `searchBudgetScale` (a binary search, ≤`BUDGET_SEARCH_STEPS`=5 iterations + a floor check + a saturation check ⇒ ≤7 calls to `buildQuadtreeAtScale`, which builds `MetricSizingField` + `PeriodicBalancedQuadtree` and reads ONLY `.leafCount()` — **no triangulation** — each probed tree is discarded after its count is read) followed by ONE `buildWallMeshAtScale` call at the chosen scale, which itself does a FRESH `buildQuadtreeAtScale` rebuild (the search never returns its tree objects, only scale+telemetry) and THEN triangulates (`triangulateQuadtree`, the plain fast path, when no general-curve features were inserted; `triangulateQuadtreeWithFeatures` — the constrained-CDT path — when they were). Added a new `WallStageTiming` (`searchMs`/`finalQuadtreeMs`/`triangulationMs`/`usedCdt`) timed at exactly these 2 call sites (search call in `buildConformingWall`; the internal quadtree-build vs. triangulate split inside `buildWallMeshAtScale`, via an optional output parameter so the function's signature/return type and every other caller stay untouched). Dev-gated by a duplicated `isDevStageTimingEnabled` (avoids a circular import: `ParametricExportComputer.ts` → `WatertightAssembly.ts` → `ConformingWall.ts`). `WatertightAssembly.ts`'s `assembleWatertight` sums the outer+inner `WallStageTiming` into its own result; `ParametricExportComputer.ts` reads it right after the existing `assembleWatertightMs` mark and folds it into `ConformingStageTimings` as 3 new sub-fields + 2 `usedCdt` flags. `assembleWatertightWithFeatures` (the opt-in corridor mesher, `flags.featureMesher`/`__pfFeatureMesher`, OFF for all 5 pilot styles) was NOT touched — out of scope, not exercised by this measurement.

**IMPACT (gitnexus, before editing):** `impact({target:"buildConformingWall", direction:"upstream", repo:"PotFoundry-Lite-v2.0"})` reported **CRITICAL** (12 impacted, 3 direct callers, 5 modules incl. BandRemesh/TierC/Bridge) at default depth — the honest reach of a function this central. Reviewed all 3 direct callers by hand before editing: `buildConformingOuterWall` (destructures 6 named fields into its own return type — a new optional field is silently dropped, zero effect), `wallsDiag` in the OTHER concurrent agent's `research/bridge/_analytic_floor_lib.ts` (reads only `.indices.length`), and `assembleWatertight` (this arm's own intended target). All 3 confirmed safe against a backward-compatible optional-field addition. `detect_changes()` afterward: risk `medium`, 3 "affected" steps all resolving to `evalPos` in `WatertightAssembly.ts` — verified via `git diff` that `evalPos`'s body has ZERO changed lines (a line-number-shift artifact from inserting code above it in the same file, not a real change).

**BYTE-IDENTITY.** All 5 styles' `vertexHash`/`indexHash` (FNV-1a) reproduce E-2026-07-09-EXPORT-STAGE-TIMING's banked hashes EXACTLY — e.g. HarmonicRipple `7fd5ce7a08783254`/`eef51df761423ead`, DragonScales `402b06455acc6e6f`/`34ee5825e0502bfb` (all 5 confirmed, full table in that entry) — across a SECOND independent capture round, on top of the FIRST round's exact triangle/vertex-count match against the original PROD-ARTIFACT-TRUTH baseline. Three independent confirmations of zero behavior change now stand.

**RESULTS — `assembleWatertight` sub-breakdown (ms, % of that style's `assembleWatertightMs`), real WebGPU, production defaults:**

| style | assembleWatertightMs | search | finalQuadtree | triangulation | outer/inner usedCdt | residual |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HarmonicRipple | 377,544 | 79,497 (21.1%) | 62,042 (16.4%) | 223,451 (**59.2%**) | false/false | 12,554 (3.3%) |
| SpiralRidges | 429,375 | 89,865 (20.9%) | 80,774 (18.8%) | 245,179 (**57.1%**) | false/false | 13,557 (3.2%) |
| GyroidManifold | 231,515 | 85,803 (**37.1%**) | 83,816 (**36.2%**) | 52,951 (22.9%) | **true**/false | 8,945 (3.9%) |
| DragonScales | 978,078 | 198,613 (20.3%) | 209,191 (21.4%) | 548,678 (**56.1%**) | false/false | 21,595 (2.2%) |
| Voronoi | 501,551 | 173,984 (**34.7%**) | 163,002 (**32.5%**) | 145,717 (29.1%) | **true**/false | 18,849 (3.8%) |
| **aggregate (Σms / Σ%)** | **2,518,063** | **627,762 (24.9%)** | **598,825 (23.8%)** | **1,215,976 (48.3%)** | 2/5 CDT | 75,501 (3.0%) |

Residual (assembleWatertightMs − the 3 buckets, 2.2–3.9%) is the config/prep work OUTSIDE both call sites — `clipFeaturesToBox`, `buildFeatureIntersector`, `computeUBias`, plus `assembleWatertight`'s own vertex-concat/index-remap/ring-sort/`orientOutward` pass. Small and not investigated further (same `otherMs`-style honesty as the parent arm, not hidden inside a bucket it doesn't belong to).

**FINDINGS:**

1. **Triangulation is the single largest sub-bucket (48.3% aggregate) — but it means TWO DIFFERENT THINGS depending on the style.** Only GyroidManifold and Voronoi (2/5) route through the constrained-CDT feature path (`triangulateQuadtreeWithFeatures` — general-curve features are present on those styles' outer wall); for them triangulation is genuinely CDT. HarmonicRipple/SpiralRidges/DragonScales (3/5) take the PLAIN fast path (`triangulateQuadtree`, no CDT) — and it is STILL their largest single sub-bucket (56–59%!). The plain quadtree→triangle-mesh assembly (transition templates, vertex packing) is not a cheap mechanical step at this scale; it is expensive in its own right, independent of CDT.

2. **The FINAL quadtree rebuild (23.8% aggregate, ~599s across the pilot) is measurably, provably REDUNDANT work at production defaults — the clearest, lowest-risk optimization candidate this arm surfaces.** `buildQuadtreeAtScale` is a pure function of (sampler, opts, pinBoundaryLevel, targetScale, featureRefine, directionalRefine, creaseRefine). `searchBudgetScale`'s `leavesAt(scale)` closure calls it with `directionalRefine` HARDCODED false on every probe (including the floor check and the final `best`/chosen-scale probe — `search.scale` is always a value `leavesAt` already built and discarded). `buildWallMeshAtScale` then calls it AGAIN at `targetScale = search.scale`, with `directionalRefine = (opts.directionalRefine ?? false) && !featurePath` — which is `false` at production defaults (`directionalRefine` is never set in the production `assemblyOpts`/`wallOpts` chain traced in E-2026-07-09-EXPORT-STAGE-TIMING). Same inputs, same deterministic function ⇒ the SAME tree, rebuilt from scratch after being thrown away moments earlier. Retaining the search's last-probed tree (or the floor/saturation-check tree, whichever `search.scale` resolves to) instead of discarding it would eliminate this bucket ENTIRELY at production defaults, by construction byte-identical — no algorithm change, no quality trade-off. (Caveat: NOT safe unconditionally — a future caller with `directionalRefine: true` genuinely needs the extra pass the search never runs; the reuse must be gated on `!(opts.directionalRefine && !featurePath)`, i.e. skip the shortcut exactly when the two builds would actually differ.)

3. **The `ConformingWall.ts` doc comment is measurably wrong at current CAD-fidelity settings.** `searchBudgetScale`'s own comment claims *"Only the quadtree is rebuilt per step (tens of ms) — triangulation runs once after."* Measured: `searchMs` implies each of the ≤14 quadtree-only rebuilds per style (≤7 probes × 2 walls) costs on the order of **several seconds, not tens of milliseconds** — HarmonicRipple's 79,497ms search alone lower-bounds the per-probe average at ≥5.7s (assuming the maximum 14 probes ran; fewer probes would raise this further), DragonScales' 198,613ms lower-bounds ≥14.2s/probe. This is 2–3 orders of magnitude beyond the documented expectation at `maxLevel:16`/`resU:resT:128`/`nRing:2048` (the CAD-fidelity floor) — the comment likely predates that floor landing. Flagging as stale documentation, not fixing here (out of scope).

**RANKED LEVERS (updated, supersedes the parent arm's "sub-instrument next" line):**
1. **Eliminate the final-quadtree-rebuild duplication (finding 2)** — ~24% of `assembleWatertight`, ~23% of total export time, PROVABLY byte-identical at production defaults, no algorithmic change. Cheapest, safest, highest-confidence win available from this measurement. **Recommended first target for a pre-registered optimization experiment**, byte-identical (`meshHash`) gated against the reference hashes banked in E-2026-07-09-EXPORT-STAGE-TIMING and re-confirmed here.
2. **Triangulation (finding 1, 48.3% aggregate)** — larger in aggregate but requires actually understanding WHY the plain fast path costs what it does at 5–8.7M triangles (not yet profiled below the `triangulateQuadtree`/`triangulateQuadtreeWithFeatures` call boundary) before proposing a change; worker-parallel CDT (tierC `parallelScorer` precedent, per the parent arm) is a candidate for the 2 CDT-path styles specifically, not the 3 plain-path styles.
3. **The genuine search cost (24.9% aggregate, minus whatever counting/comparison work can't be avoided)** — hardest lever: fewer/cheaper probes is an algorithm change (risk to the ±10% `BUDGET_TOLERANCE` band), not a free deduplication.

**CAVEATS:** (a) Same shared-machine caveat as the parent arm — a second Claude session (commit `2d72a56f`, co-authored "Claude Fable 5") was concurrently committing to this exact working tree during this arm, including hunks in `ConformingWall.ts`/`WatertightAssembly.ts`/`ParametricExportComputer.ts` (the `E-2026-07-09-ANALYTIC-FLOOR` `curvatureFloor`/`maxKappa` wiring) adjacent to but non-overlapping with this arm's hunks — confirmed via diff review; both sets of changes compile, lint, and test clean together. Their commit's message self-documents the shared-tree sweep. Absolute totals (`totalMs`: HarmonicRipple 402s / SpiralRidges 455s / GyroidManifold 237s / DragonScales 990s / Voronoi 514s this round) are NOT directly comparable to the parent arm's round for contention reasons already stated there — the byte-identical hashes are the load-bearing evidence, not the wall-clock deltas. (b) A capture-script browser crash (`Target page ... has been closed`, cause unconfirmed — likely GPU/memory contention from the concurrent session, not a code defect) killed the run after HarmonicRipple; retried the remaining 4 styles in a fresh browser and all completed clean with byte-identical hashes, so the reported numbers are genuine, just gathered across 2 sub-runs rather than 1. (c) The residual (finding table, 2.2–3.9%) is not further decomposed — flagged, not chased, matching the audit-first "report the gap honestly" convention.

**LEDGER:** src (additive, DEV-gated, byte-identical off) `src/renderers/webgpu/parametric/conforming/ConformingWall.ts` (+`WallStageTiming`, `isDevWallStageTimingEnabled`, timing around `searchBudgetScale`'s call site + `buildWallMeshAtScale`'s internal quadtree/triangulate split, `stageTiming` on `ConformingWallResult`), `WatertightAssembly.ts` (+`stageTiming` summed onto `WatertightAssemblyResult`), `ParametricExportComputer.ts` (+5 fields on `ConformingStageTimings`, read from `asm.stageTiming` right after the existing `assembleWatertightMs` mark). `windowHook.ts` unchanged — `FidelityStageTimingDiagnostics extends ConformingStageTimings` inherits the new fields automatically. Capture: same `e2e/_export_stage_timing_capture.mjs`. Data `research/exchange/_export_stage_timing/<style>.json` (overwritten in place with the richer per-style JSON — gitignored, numbers inlined above and in the parent entry). ## E-2026-07-10-ANALYTIC-FLOOR-MASKED — crest-band-MASKED analytic floor via FINE sizing-grid evaluation: drive the SpiralRidges every-facet ≤0.01 close from 1.935× to ≤1.5× [PRE-REGISTERED — kill-criteria committed BEFORE measuring]

**FRAME (follow-up to §E-2026-07-09-ANALYTIC-FLOOR, which CLOSED fidelity and FIRED KILL-2).** The parent arm proved the mechanism (every-facet ≤0.01 Newton: 3,140 over/0.0239 → 0 over/0.009985; coverage 0.0353 → 0.0088) at 11,004,336 tris = 1.935× — over the ≤1.5× gate (8,530,251). DESIGN ANALYSIS of the measured cost (this entry's basis, no new measurement): (1) **the smear is the GRID, not the math** — the pointwise closed-form κ already decays off-crest naturally (flank κ ≈ the bare-profile ~0.02 mm⁻¹ ⇒ sagitta h > maxEdge ⇒ no demanded refinement), but the floor is evaluated on the sizing lattice, and at the production 128² the node pitch is 2.7mm against a 9.6mm crest spacing (36 loci / 346mm circumference) — the ±1-node sup window + bilinear interpolation lift ≥4-node (~10.8mm) spans per locus, i.e. essentially the WHOLE circumference ⇒ the parent arm's near-uniform densification. The "crest-band mask" is therefore realized by RESOLUTION: evaluate the SAME floor (no formula change — `AnalyticCurvatureFloor` is already res-parametric, sup window = ±1 node at the given res) on a finer sizing grid, and its natural |f″| support emerges. (2) **ANALYTIC-PRIOR CORRECTION (banked):** the parent FRAME's naive polar estimate "joint-crest κ ≈ 0.6 mm⁻¹" is REFUTED by the parent's own measurements — the outer wall saturating its 8M 'cap' share back-solves to an effective uniform h ≈ 0.11mm ⇒ true crest κ ≈ 2.0–2.4 mm⁻¹, i.e. AT/NEAR the maxKappa cap 2.4 (cross terms + joint main×groove alignment the naive estimate dropped; the floor unit test's gridMax ∈ (0.2, 2.4) window is consistent). Crest cells therefore sit near minEdge-adjacent h ≈ 0.10–0.11mm — the close is real but each lifted mm² is ~2.5× denser than the baseline mean (h̄ ≈ 0.176mm), which is exactly why band WIDTH is the whole cost story. (3) The budget-search coherence (floor flows through `buildQuadtreeAtScale` into `leavesAt`) and the H0 byte-identity instrument are inherited from the parent arm unchanged.

**HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable):** evaluating the SpiralRidges analytic floor on a finer sizing lattice (resU 512, resT 128; flag-ON only) narrows the lifted bands to ≈ the true crest support (core ±0.68mm + gradeRatio-2 halo ~2mm/side per locus), holding the every-facet ≤0.01 Newton close while bringing the full-pot count to ≤1.5× (predicted full ∈ [6.0M, 7.6M] = 1.06–1.34×; predicted worst flagged Newton ≤ 0.007; predicted coverage max ≤ 0.009).

**METHOD (ordered; instruments committed BEFORE running).**
1. **FRAME.** The prior arm summed `outer.stageTiming + inner.stageTiming` into one number, explicitly flagging that this "hides that features only ever land on the outer wall" and left a 2.2–3.9%-of-bucket residual unattributed (config prep + vertex/index array assembly + `orientOutward`, everything `assembleWatertight` does OUTSIDE either wall's `buildConformingWall` call). **IMPACT:** `impact({target:"assembleWatertight", direction:"upstream", repo:"PotFoundry-Lite-v2.0"})` → **HIGH** (8 direct callers: 6 in the BandRemesh feature-mesher subsystem — `assembleWatertightWithFeatures[Debug]`, `integrateSingleBand`, `realFeatureCorridor[Multi/PerLoop]` — which call the plain `assembleWatertight` as a base helper; 1 research probe (`buildProductionTwin`); this arm's own `compute()` target). ## E-2026-07-10-TRIANGULATION-SUBTIMING — sub-instrument `triangulationMs` itself (48–90% of `assembleWatertightMs` depending on style/CDT-path): prep / grid-line registry / the per-leaf emission loop / tolerance weld / seam close (user-directed follow-up) [MEASURED — instrumentation only, no optimization authored in this arm]

**FRAME.** Third and (for now) final descent into `assembleWatertight`: PROD-ARTIFACT-TRUTH → EXPORT-STAGE-TIMING found `assembleWatertight` ≈97% of total → ASSEMBLEWATERTIGHT-SUBTIMING split it into search/finalQuadtree/triangulation (triangulation itself 22.9–59.2% of the bucket) → ASSEMBLEWATERTIGHT-PERWALL separated outer/inner and closed the residual to <0.3% → this arm opens `triangulationMs` itself, the largest still-opaque number. Both triangulators share a superficially similar structure (leaf enumeration → grid-line registry → per-leaf emission → seam-close), but `triangulateQuadtreeWithFeatures` (the CDT path — see `TRI_SOURCE.FCT_FEATURE_CDT`, `ConstrainedCellTriangulator`) additionally does feature-point snapping, spatial bucketing, rail force-registration, feature-cell classification, and a tolerance weld pass the plain path (`triangulateQuadtree`) never runs.

Phase boundaries: `prepMs` = leaf enum + per-leaf geometry (feature path: + snap/bucket/rails); `registryMs` = grid-line registry construction (PASS A; feature path: + PASS A0 directional pass + per-cell feature classification); `emitMs` = the main per-leaf loop (PASS B — where the actual `triangulateConstrainedCell` CDT calls live on the feature path); `weldMs` = the float-jitter tolerance weld (feature path ONLY — always 0 on the plain path, there is no such step there); `seamCloseMs` = the shared u=1→u=0 merge + index compaction. `ConformingWall.ts`'s `WallStageTiming` gained one more optional field, `triangulationDetail?: TriangulationStageTiming`, copied straight from the triangulator's own return value at both existing call sites — no changes needed in `WatertightAssembly.ts`, `ParametricExportComputer.ts`, or `windowHook.ts` (all three already carry the FULL `WallStageTiming` object by reference from the E-2026-07-10-ASSEMBLEWATERTIGHT-PERWALL restructuring, so a new nested field on it propagates automatically — that restructuring's extensibility paid off immediately).

Also: the prior arm's Voronoi-only `reusedSearchQuadtree`/`finalQuadtreeMs:0` anomaly is now UNIVERSAL — all 10 wall-builds (5 styles × 2 walls) show `reusedSearchQuadtree: true` and `finalQuadtreeMs: 0` this round. **FINDINGS:**

1. **`emit` — the main per-leaf triangulation loop (PASS B) — is overwhelmingly dominant: 90.6% of triangulation time in aggregate, 95.2% on the 8 non-CDT walls specifically.** This is the sharpest, most lopsided split found across all three descents into `assembleWatertight` (94–99% → 22–59% → now 90–97%). Concretely: for the 8 walls that never hit the CDT path, virtually the ENTIRE triangulation cost is the leaf-by-leaf work — per-side split-flag probes (`sideHasFiner`), reading the union of edge-subdivision points from the grid-line registry, building the CCW boundary polygon, and the diagonal/fan/Klincsek-DP triangulation choice with its `vertexIndex` Map-based dedup. Leaf enumeration (`prep`, 2.1–8.7%) and the registry CONSTRUCTION itself (as opposed to reading it, which happens inside emit — `registry`, 0.5–4.1% on non-CDT walls) are comparatively cheap; the cost is in walking every leaf and deciding/emitting its triangles, not in the bookkeeping around it.
2. **The tolerance weld is a REAL, sometimes-dominant cost — but ONLY on the CDT path, and its share varies wildly between the two CDT styles measured.** Weld is exactly 0 on all 8 non-CDT walls (there is no such step there — confirmed structurally, not just measured near-zero). On the 2 CDT walls it is 18.6% (Voronoi) to **41.3% (GyroidManifold — where it is the SINGLE LARGEST sub-bucket, bigger than emit itself)**. GyroidManifold's CDT wall and Voronoi's CDT wall have qualitatively DIFFERENT cost profiles: GyroidManifold is weld-dominated (41.3% weld vs. 30.3% emit), Voronoi is emit-dominated (71.2% emit vs. 18.6% weld) with a much bigger registry share too (7.0% vs. GyroidManifold's 19.1% — note these percentages are of DIFFERENT-sized wholes, GyroidManifold's CDT wall is 8.5× smaller than Voronoi's). Plausible mechanism (not verified in this arm): GyroidManifold's TPMS level-set features vs. Voronoi's cell-hash features likely produce very different feature-point/near-edge-duplicate DENSITY, and `weldMs`'s cost is presumably driven by vertex COUNT there (spatial-hash + 3×3 neighbour sweep per vertex), not feature-curve complexity per se — a hypothesis for a future arm, not this one.
3. **`registry` costs meaningfully more on CDT walls (4.6–14.3k ms) than on plain walls (0.6–2.2k ms), consistent with what it actually does differently there** — PASS A's per-cell feature classification (boundary points + interior + constraints, `LeafData`) vs. the plain path's simple 4-corner registration. Still small in absolute terms next to emit/weld.
4. **`seamClose` is uniformly negligible (0.1–1.8%, mostly <0.5%)** on every wall — not worth any further attention.

**WHAT THIS THREE-ARM SERIES NOW EXPLAINS, END TO END (chained percentages, illustrative — exact figures vary by style):** of a production default export's total wall-clock, ~97% is `assembleWatertight` (EXPORT-STAGE-TIMING) → of THAT, roughly half is outer-wall + half is inner-wall triangulation-dominated work with ~3% array-packing (ASSEMBLEWATERTIGHT-PERWALL) → of a wall's OWN triangulation time, ~90–95% (non-CDT) or 30–71% (CDT, weld competing) is the PASS B emission loop (this arm). Composing the middle figures: **the PASS B emission loop alone is roughly 40–55% of a typical style's ENTIRE export wall-clock time** (back-of-envelope: ~97% × ~50%(wall share, search+finalQ+tri only, finalQ now ≈0) × ~90–95%(non-CDT emit share) ≈ 45–50%, using this round's own numbers rather than re-deriving from the chain — not independently re-verified as one product in this arm, offered as orientation, not a new measured figure).

**NEXT (not started in this arm; the honest floor of this measurement series):** `emit`'s internal cost is now the single largest still-opaque number in the whole pipeline (≈45–50% of total export time by the estimate above). It is NOT sub-instrumented further here — the natural next question is what INSIDE the per-leaf loop costs the most: the `sideHasFiner`/`uColHasFiner` split-flag probes (called up to 4×/leaf, each an O(maxLevel) scan), the `vertexIndex` Map-based dedup (a `Map<number,number>` lookup+insert per emitted vertex), or the triangulation-choice logic itself (`metricLen2`/`emitShapedTransition`/Klincsek DP on anisotropic cells). This would require literal per-call-site profiling (`console.time` around each probe type would itself distort a hot loop called millions of times) — likely the point where dev-gated wall-clock bucket timing, the technique this whole series has used, stops being the right tool and a sampling profiler (Chrome DevTools CPU profile, taken on a real capture run) becomes the better next instrument. Flagging the tool-choice question explicitly rather than mechanically continuing the same technique past its useful range.

## E-2026-07-10-EMIT-CPU-PROFILE — Chrome DevTools sampling CPU profile of one production-default export, to find what's actually hot inside the wall-clock buckets this series can no longer usefully subdivide [MEASURED — read-only capture, no src/ edit at all]

**FRAME.** E-2026-07-10-TRIANGULATION-SUBTIMING closed with an explicit tool-choice call: `emit`'s internal cost (≈45–50% of a style's total export time by that arm's own estimate) is the largest still-opaque number in the pipeline, but a loop invoked per-leaf across millions of leaves is the wrong target for MORE wall-clock `console.time` bucketing — the instrumentation itself would distort what it measures. This arm switches instruments: a real V8 sampling CPU profile via the Chrome DevTools Protocol `Profiler` domain, which samples the call stack at a fixed interval (default 1kHz) rather than timing named regions, so it can attribute cost to a function without touching its code at all.

**METHOD.** New capture `e2e/_export_cpu_profile.mjs`: Playwright launches real-WebGPU Chromium (same pattern as every prior capture in this series), opens a CDP session (`page.context().newCDPSession(page)`), `Profiler.enable` + `Profiler.start`, drives ONE production-default export via the existing `window.__pfFidelity.diagnoseStageTimings()` (so this run's own wall-clock bucket numbers are captured in the SAME execution for direct cross-reference — no separate run needed), `Profiler.stop` (returns the standard `.cpuprofile` JSON: a node tree keyed by `callFrame` with `hitCount` = samples where that node was top-of-stack, i.e. SELF time). Self time per function is aggregated as `(hitCount / totalHitCount) × profiledDurationMs`, grouped by `functionName@file:line` (V8 emits a distinct node per call-tree position, so nodes for the SAME function are summed). Profiled style: **GyroidManifold** (the fastest pilot style that still exercises BOTH the plain triangulator (inner wall) and the constrained-CDT path (outer wall, `usedCdt:true`) in one build — one capture, both code paths). No source file was edited for this arm — a CPU profiler needs no code changes to attribute cost, unlike every prior arm in this series.

**BYTE-IDENTITY.** Same hash as every predecessor arm (`56872d5e4292d78c`/`5aa82d85f6b28ed3`) — the 6th confirmation, though trivially expected here since NOTHING was edited.

**RESULTS — top self-time functions (192,501ms profiled, 142,682 samples, 685 call-tree nodes):**

| rank | function | file:line | self ms | % of total profiled time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **`hasLeaf`** | `PeriodicBalancedQuadtree.ts:203` | 72,223.5 | **37.5%** |
| 2 | `readH` | `QuadtreeTriangulator.ts:266` | 20,121.4 | 10.5% |
| 3 | *(garbage collector)* | native | 17,657.9 | 9.2% |
| 4 | `triangulateQuadtreeWithFeatures` (self, i.e. inline loop body) | `FeatureConformingTriangulator.ts:152` | 11,351.9 | 5.9% |
| 5 | `cellOfKey` | `PeriodicBalancedQuadtree.ts:179` | 9,526.4 | 4.9% |
| 6 | `cellKey` | `PeriodicBalancedQuadtree.ts:2` | 8,869.4 | 4.6% |
| 7 | `hasCell` | `FeatureConformingTriangulator.ts:184` | 6,740.4 | 3.5% |

| 9 | `topologyMetric` | `fidelity/metrics.ts:649` | 5,192.9 | 2.7% |

| 12 | `hasFinerThanOneLevelNeighbour` | `PeriodicBalancedQuadtree.ts:310` | 2,961.4 | 1.5% |
| — | `vertexIndex` (both triangulators, combined) | — | 1,816.0 | 0.9% |

**THE FINDING (one mechanism, 56% of the whole export):** `hasLeaf`/`cellOfKey`/`cellKey`/`addLeaf`/`hasFinerThanOneLevelNeighbour`/`finestNeighbourLevel`/`enforcePinnedBoundary` — every hot function in `PeriodicBalancedQuadtree.ts` — sum to **97,076.4ms, 50.4% of the entire profiled export**. Plus the triangulators' OWN local existence checks, `has` (`QuadtreeTriangulator.ts`) and `hasCell` (`FeatureConformingTriangulator.ts`): **+10,781.1ms. Total: 107,857.5ms — 56.0% of the whole export's CPU time**, traced to ONE mechanism, implemented independently 3 times:

```ts
// PeriodicBalancedQuadtree.ts:85-87 (module-level function)
function cellKey(level: number, it: number, eUL: number, iu: number): string {
  return `${level}:${it}:${eUL}:${iu}`;
}
// :338-343 — called from finestNeighbourLevel (×3 call sites) during
// enforcePinnedBoundary's balance pass, over EVERY leaf, potentially
// multiple passes until the tree stabilizes:
private hasLeaf(level: number, iu: number, it: number, uExtra = 0): boolean {
  ...
  return this.leafSet.has(cellKey(level, it, eUL, wu));  // Set<string>
}
```
`QuadtreeTriangulator.ts`'s local `has` closure and `FeatureConformingTriangulator.ts`'s local `hasCell` closure independently re-implement the EXACT same pattern (`cellSet.add(\`${l.level}:${it}:${eUL}:${iu}\`)`, `Set<string>`) rather than sharing `cellKey`/`hasLeaf` — three separate implementations of "build a template-literal string, then Set-lookup it," called per-leaf, per-side, per-balance-pass. Every call ALLOCATES a new string (template-literal interpolation is not free) and then hashes it for the Set lookup — versus a numeric key, which V8 can hash/compare with no allocation at all. The **17,657.9ms (9.2%) spent in the garbage collector** is the direct, visible cost of that allocation churn — GC time this large on a computation with no obviously-large data structures being discarded is itself a symptom pointing at exactly this kind of per-call small-object (string) allocation.

**Every method touched is `private`** (confirmed: `leaves()` and `uBias()` are the ONLY public methods on `PeriodicBalancedQuadtree` — grepped every method signature in the file) — so `hasLeaf`'s cost is provably ENTIRELY inside quadtree construction/balancing (the `search` bucket from ASSEMBLEWATERTIGHT-SUBTIMING), never inside triangulation. Cross-checked against THIS SAME RUN's own `diagnoseStageTimings()` bucket numbers (captured in the identical execution): `search` (outer 67,866.7ms + inner 39,910.9ms) = 107,777.6ms — `hasLeaf` alone is **67.0% of that**, and the FULL `PeriodicBalancedQuadtree.ts` total (97,076.4ms) is **90.1% of the ENTIRE search bucket**. This is the mechanistic answer the E-2026-07-09-EXPORT-STAGE-TIMING arm's stale-doc-comment finding ("tens of ms" per quadtree rebuild, measured to be seconds) was missing: search costs what it does because the 2:1-balance refinement's neighbour-existence checks are string-keyed.

**Notably NOT the bottleneck, despite being a plausible suspect:** `vertexIndex` (the `Map<number,number>`-based vertex-dedup used by BOTH triangulators during emission) is only 0.9% combined (1,816ms) — it uses a NUMERIC key (the quantized `(u,t)` pair packed into one number) and is cheap exactly because it avoids the string-key pattern above. This is a working, already-in-the-codebase counter-example proving the fix direction: `QuadtreeTriangulator.ts`'s OWN grid-line registry (`regH`/`regV`, keyed by `Math.round(x * QSCALE)` — a plain number) is ALSO numeric-keyed and cheap per-lookup (`readH`/`readV`'s cost — 12.2% combined — comes from CALL VOLUME across millions of leaf-sides, not per-call overhead; contrast with `hasLeaf` at comparable-or-lower call volume but 3× the cost).

**NEXT (not started in this arm — an optimization hypothesis with strong evidence, not an implemented or verified fix):** replace the string-templated `cellKey`/local `cellSet` keys with a packed-integer encoding. `level`, `it`, `eUL`, `iu` are all small, bounded non-negative integers (`level`/`eUL` ≤ `maxLevel`=16 at the CAD-fidelity floor; `it`/`iu` ≤ 2^level) — they fit in a packed `number` (bit-shift) or a single `BigInt`/two-`number` pair if precision demands it, turning three `Set<string>`/`Map<string,...>` structures into `Set<number>`/`Map<number,...>`. This is NOT a novel technique for this codebase — `QuadtreeTriangulator.ts`'s own grid-line registry already proves the pattern works here. A future arm implementing this MUST run a pre-registered byte-identical (`meshHash`) gate against the reference hashes banked across this whole series (5 styles, now 6 confirmations) before any claim of speedup — the encoding must be provably collision-free across the SAME (level,it,eUL,iu) domain the string version covers exactly, or the quadtree's correctness (not just its speed) is at risk.

**LEDGER:** NEW file `e2e/_export_cpu_profile.mjs` (capture + self-time-by-function aggregation, no src/ touched). Data `research/exchange/_cpu_profile/GyroidManifold.cpuprofile` (raw V8 profile — loadable in Chrome DevTools > Performance, or `chrome://inspect` > a target's Profiler tab, for an interactive flame graph) + `GyroidManifold_hotspots.json` (full ranked self-time table, this entry shows top 12) + `GyroidManifold_timings.json` (this SAME run's wall-clock buckets, for the cross-reference above) — all gitignored under `research/exchange/`, numbers inlined here. No `gitnexus impact()` run — no symbol was edited. Commit [this].

## E-2026-07-10-INTKEY-SWAP — FIX the E-2026-07-10-EMIT-CPU-PROFILE hotspot: replace the per-leaf template-literal STRING cell keys (`Set<string>`/`Map<string,string>`) with a collision-free packed-INTEGER codec across the quadtree + both triangulators [OPTIMIZATION — byte-identical gate PASSED, ~2-3× on the affected path]

**FRAME (the first OPTIMIZATION arm of this measurement series — audit-first paid off).** E-2026-07-10-EMIT-CPU-PROFILE (a real V8 sampling profile) traced ~56% of a production GyroidManifold export's CPU to ONE mechanism implemented three times: build a template-literal string key (`${level}:${it}:${eUL}:${iu}`) per cell, then `Set<string>.has/add` it — `hasLeaf`/`cellKey`/`cellOfKey` in `PeriodicBalancedQuadtree.ts` (50.4%) + the triangulators' own `has`/`hasCell` re-implementations (5.6%), plus 9.2% GC churning the per-call string allocations. That arm named the fix (packed-integer keys, "the pattern already sits one file away in the numeric-keyed `regH`/`regV` registry") and pre-registered the gate: *"MUST run a pre-registered byte-identical (`meshHash`) gate ... the encoding must be provably collision-free."* This arm executes it, TDD.

**THE INVARIANT + TDD.** A numeric key that COLLIDES would silently merge two distinct quadtree leaves and corrupt the mesh (not just slow it) — so the codec is a BIJECTION on the same (level, it, uExtra, iu) domain the string covered. New `conforming/QuadtreeCellKeyCodec.ts` packs each field into its own bit-range sized to the tree's actual bounds; `conforming/QuadtreeCellKeyCodec.test.ts` (written FIRST, RED verified — module absent — before GREEN) proves round-trip + distinctness (exhaustive at low levels, boundary+strided sampled higher, across production + stress configs), safe-integer range, uEff equivalence classes, and that a pathological config THROWS rather than silently overflows. 15/15. Keys store `uExtra ∈ [0, MAX_U_EXTRA]` (3 bits) not the derived `eUL` (bijective for fixed uBias ⇒ identical equivalence classes, ~44 bits total for production) — `MAX_U_EXTRA` in all three files now SOURCES from the codec constant so the field width can't drift.

**IMPACT (gitnexus, before editing):** `cellKey` LOW (4 callers, all in-file — module-private); `PeriodicBalancedQuadtree` class MEDIUM but only via its public `leaves()`/`uBias()` (unchanged — I changed only the internal `leafSet`/`uByEffective` representation); the two triangulators HIGH (feature-mesher subsystem callers) but the key structures are file-internal. `PeriodicBalancedQuadtree.ts` was CLEAN in the working tree (no concurrent editor) — verified before touching it.

**A REAL BUG THE TDD CAUGHT (the load-bearing value of the full unit suite).** First wiring passed the pinned-hash `ConformingWall` byte-identical gate (17/17) BUT failed 2 `PeriodicBalancedQuadtree.test.ts` `minUniformLevel` tests. Root cause: the test uses `maxLevel 7 / pinBoundaryLevel 8`, and `enforcePinnedBoundary` splits the boundary rows to EXACTLY pinBoundaryLevel — which CAN exceed maxLevel. My codec sized `it` to maxLevel=7 bits (holds it<128); a level-8 boundary cell has it up to 255 → field overflow → silent collision → a missing column. Production never trips it (there pin=log2(nRing)−uBias=11 < maxLevel=16, which is exactly why the pinned-hash gate — a production config — passed clean and MISSED it). Fix: size the codec to `max(maxLevel, pinBoundaryLevel)`. The pre-existing quadtree unit tests were the regression net the production-config hash gate could not be. (`refine()` caps every other split at `levelCap ≤ maxLevel`, and `minUniformLevel` is itself `min(_, maxLevel)`, so that bound provably covers every cell level.)

**A SECOND SUBTLETY (the feature path).** `FeatureConformingTriangulator`'s `snapToCellEdge` probes `hasCell` with UNBOUNDED uExtra (walks every coarser level under a fixed eUL), which the string key tolerated (it stored eUL literally) but a bounded uExtra field would overflow. A real leaf never has uExtra ∉ [0, MAX_U_EXTRA], so such a probe never matched the string set either ⇒ guard `if (uExtra < 0 || uExtra > MAX_U_EXTRA) return false` BEFORE packing — exactly equivalent, collision-safe. Added to both triangulators' lookups (a no-op in the plain path where callers are already guarded; load-bearing in the feature path).

## E-2026-07-12-FOLDCLOSE — Gyroid pinned-fold "midline-embed + sparse across-fold escalation" (region-core fold branch)

**HYPOTHESIS.** Embedding the steepest-slope midline `|val|=0.1425` contour into the Gyroid featureLine set (ADDED to the doubled band-edge pair) + driving verdict-driven SPARSE across-fold escalation of the pinned cell + near-twins CLOSES the pinned MAX facet @ (u=0.655,t=0.879) (GPU-truth 0.7241mm) to ≤0.01 at bounded tri cost, watertight.

**VERDICT: PREMISE-VOID + COVERAGE-EXTENSION-INSUFFICIENT.** Two findings:

1. **The band-edge baseline does NOT reproduce the 0.72 fold — it already resolves that region.** On the CPU-analytic production kernel (`buildConformingWall`, band-edge contours = the P2.5b/c config, 2,242,984 outer tris) the pinned-cell facet reads **0.0041mm** (Newton; radial 0.0125) at **level 11**, region worst (±0.05 (u,t) box) **0.0135mm**, nonMan 0. The 53× gap to the GPU 0.7241 is NOT the ~1.6× CPU-under-read — it is a FEATURE-SET difference: the outer band-edge contour `|val|=0.15` passes within **0.38 t-cells / 0.76 u-cells** of the pinned point (mid 0.1425 is ~0.9 t-cell / 1.8 u-cell away), so `featureLevel`-11 already covers the pinned cell. The 0.7241 belongs to production's real `val=0` plateau feature set (|val|≈0.155 away ⇒ walls UNCOVERED). **The band-edge override is itself the wall-coverage fix; it closes the fold before any midline is added.**

2. **Midline embed + sparse across-fold escalation does NOT move the remaining region residual.** mid-embed (|val|=0.1425 added): pinned 0.0041 (unchanged), region 0.0135→**0.0133**, **+6.13% tris**, nonMan 0. mid-esc L12/L14/L16: pinned improves marginally 0.0041→**0.0024** (already sub-tol), region worst **PINNED at 0.01332 and DEPTH-INVARIANT** — it is already at **level 15** (a level-15 smooth fold chord would be O(L²)≈1e-8; this is not a fold), +6.2–7.2% tris. Cross-attribution control (per-cell cross injected AT the pinned point + esc L16): region **identical 0.01332** ⇒ NOT a coverage-reach problem. The 0.01332 residual (locus 0.6496,0.8496) is the P2.5b-class **sliver/junction "rechord/K2" floor**, not the pinned fold, and the midline mechanism does not touch it.

**KILL-CRITERION (pre-registered):** FOLD-CLOSEABLE iff pinned & region worst ≤0.01, nonMan 0, added tris ≤+10%. Result: pinned was already ≤0.01 in baseline (nothing to close on this surface); region residual did NOT close (0.0135→0.0133). Cost bounded (+6-7%, NOT the +113% P2.5 blow-up), watertight throughout — the mechanism is well-behaved on cost/topology, it just does not address this residual.

**RECOMMENDATION.** (a) To attack the real GPU 0.72 fold, the baseline MUST use production's `val=0` feature set (walls uncovered) — then band-edge/mid embedding is expected to close it; the finding is the band-edge override ALREADY does. (b) The depth-invariant 0.01332 @ L15 region residual is the true remaining region-core target and is sliver/junction-class — it needs the P2.5b K2/rechord mechanism, not midline embedding.

3. **The non-certified population is ANTI-correlated with the order-1 graph.** On-graph (<= 1 cell diag): 11 of 1,874 = **0.6%** (gate wanted >=95%). Certified cells are on-graph at 22.7% — i.e. the cells the screen struggles with are FARTHER from the bisectors (dist/diag p50 6.230) than the ones it certifies (p50 2.430).
4. **The real obstruction is the SITE CONE (f1=0, the sqrt-at-0 cusp), not the bisector kink.** 1,788 of 1,874 non-certified cells (**95.4%**) lie within one cell diagonal of a lattice site centre; site-dist/diag p50 **0.538** (non-certified) vs **6.400** (certified) — a ~12x separation.
5. **The "site cones quiet in both modes" clause is refuted outright.** The screen REFUSES (returns null, no bound) on exactly 128 cells = 64 sites x 2 triangles, and 128/128 (100.0%) are within one cell diagonal of a site centre (worst 0.489 diag). Refusal count is INVARIANT at 128 across base grids 16x4 / 64x8 / 256x32 / 1024x128 — a fixed locus, not a size effect.
6. **Soundness self-check GREEN (P-INV-2):** min slack +0.1510 um >= 0 over all 269,640 cells.

**INSTRUMENT CORRECTION (blocks P1 as literally worded):** spec P1 is phrased over "Clarke-fired cells", but `getLastScreenClarkeFired()` is a TAPE-GLOBAL boolean (`validatedResidualProgram.ts:2100` — "set when a min/max/abs node takes its Clarke subgradient branch during a tape run"), with no per-node attribution. The Voronoi tape's smoothstep CLAMPS are themselves min/max nodes, so the flag reads **100.0% on every cell** and carries zero stratum information. Testing P1 through that flag is impossible; the overlay therefore gates on the DISPOSITION-based proxy (subdivide|depthcap = "screen could not certify"), which is what the hang actually means. Stratum-keyed telemetry is plan phase S4 — it is a PREREQUISITE for S0's own gate, not a later nicety.

**RECONCILIATION HYPOTHESIS (untested, for spec revision):** the fast screen terminates, but at the 128 cone cells it REFUSES, and `continuousMappedPatchDistance` (:983-987) escalates a null fast screen to the EXACT evaluator rather than stopping. The reported "certification hangs" is therefore plausibly the exact-evaluator escalation at 64 site cones, NOT Clarke-hull subdivision on bisectors. Confirming this needs a real cMPD certification run and is the natural first task of the revised plan.

**CONSEQUENCE FOR THE CAMPAIGN:** S1's pivot+one-sided-defect rule targets `min`/`max`/`abs` Clarke hulls on creases. That is not the binding constraint measured here. The measured constraint is a CUSP, whose spec-designated mechanism (section 7 stratification table) is "pinned vertex + value-hull cells (cone-fan on the mesh side)" — a different lever, with in-repo precedent (`__pfDsConeFan`, E-2026-07-20 DS ring close).

**SCOPE CAVEATS (honest):** measured on the fast screen only (not a full cMPD certification); bubble mode only (v_morph 0) — web mode (P2, order-2 edges) NOT yet run; single relief value v_relief=0.04; outer-wall patch only; oracleRes 4 (falsifier resolution, adequate for disposition but not for a tight slack quantile claim).

**LEDGER.** Harness (additive, money-metrics unchanged): `research/bridge/_gothicScreenSlackAudit.test.ts` — per-cell CSV of EVERY VISITED cell with its accept/subdivide/depthcap/refused disposition (`PF_SLACK_CSV`, capped `PF_SLACK_CSV_MAX`); emitting only accepted leaves, as the plan first specified, would have structurally hidden the entire non-certified population. NEW (analysis-only, no kernel code runs): `research/bridge/_strataFiredMapOverlay.test.ts` (`PF_STRATA_OVERLAY=1`, `PF_STRATA_CSV`). Runner: `vitest.strata.config.ts`. Evidence: `research/bridge/out/strata_s0_deep.{csv,txt}`, `research/bridge/out/strata_s0_overlay_deep.txt`. Reused READ-ONLY: `voronoiBisectorSegmentsUv` / `voronoiCenterCellular` / `voronoiNearestCenterId` (`voronoiBisectorGuides.ts`), `compileValidatedResidualProgram` / `fastEncloseCompiledValidatedResidualProgram` (`validatedResidualProgram.ts`).

## E-2026-07-23-STRATA001-S0-CERTIFY (STRATA-001 S0 increment 2: does the REAL certifier hang on Voronoi? bubble vs web, budget + depth sweeps) [MEASURE-ONLY; NO kernel edit; gate PF_STRATA_CERTIFY]

**HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable):** the spec's founding [MEASURED] claim "raising the triangle budget does not terminate the Voronoi screen (certification hangs)" reproduces in the REAL certifier (`certifyContinuousMappedPatchDistance`), and its error CODE attributes the mechanism: `RESOURCE_LIMIT` = the spec's Clarke-hull cell blow-up, `EVALUATOR_REFUSED` = the site-cone cusp found in increment 1, deadline = wall-clock starvation.

**KILL-CRITERION (pre-registered):** the spec's root cause survives only if the failure is `RESOURCE_LIMIT`/timeout AND the failing locus is a kink stratum AND the failure is insensitive to loosening the tolerance (an h-independent bound cannot be bought off with budget).

**VERDICT: the hang does NOT exist; the real failure is a budget-INVARIANT `INCONCLUSIVE` at the depth cap, which is a certifier behaviour, not a mesh property.**

Config: Voronoi `v_relief 0.04`, H32/OD30/drain6, `tessellateAnnularRadialSolidTargetForCertification` angularLog2 8 / walls verticalLog2 7, per-patch isolation, 90-300 s deadline/patch.

1. **BUBBLE mode fully certifies — no hang.** All six patches OK in ~99 s (outer-wall `upperPm=9499530`, 74,960 cells, maxDepth 8, 39 s; inner 75,592/depth 8; top-rim 53,608; bottom-under 40,704; bottom-top 16,920; drain-wall 870/depth 15). Reproduced independently via the pre-existing `PF_SLICE11_VOR_PP` probe. The 128 site-cone REFUSALS found in increment 1 are absorbed by the exact-evaluator escalation (cMPD:983-987) without stalling.
2. **WEB mode (v_morph 1) fails on both walls — but as `INCONCLUSIVE`, in 3-12 s, never `RESOURCE_LIMIT` and never a timeout.** outer-wall: `Residual upper 9500023 pm exceeds 9500000 pm at maximum depth`, tri 102472, depth 24, uv (0.14063,0.05469).
3. **The failing cells lie ON the ORDER-1 bisector graph**, distance **0.0014 lattice-cell units** for the cell centroid (vertices ~0.03), vs **0.41** cells to the nearest site cone. Inner-wall likewise (0.052 vs 0.66). This REFUTES the spec section 3 claim that the web centerline is benign by smoothstep s'(0)=0 attenuation — web fails exactly there — and gives NO support to prediction P2 (web kinks on the order-2 stratum); the order-2 graph is not implicated by this evidence.
4. **Depth sweep — section 3's h-INDEPENDENCE claim is REFUTED.** Same cell, maxDepth 24 -> 30 (64x finer h): residual upper falls **9,500,023 -> 9,500,001 pm** (23 pm over -> 1 pm over). A Clarke-hull-pinned bound would not move at all.
5. **Budget sweep — the failure is INVARIANT to tolerance.** budget 9,500,000 -> fail at 9,500,023 (**+23 pm**); budget 9,700,000 -> fail at 9,700,023 (**+23 pm**, same triangle 102472, same UV); budget 20,000,000 -> fail at 20,000,017 (**+17 pm**, triangle 105120). Doubling the tolerance does not certify. A genuine geometric error of ~9.5 um would certify trivially at 20 um, so **the failing cell's reported residual is not a physical property of the mesh**.
6. **Density sweep does not fix it either** — walls verticalLog2 7 -> 8 moves the failure to a different triangle (175068) at the same order of overshoot (+17 pm).
7. **`targetToMeshUpperPm` is NOT a fidelity measurement.** By construction (cMPD:1025-1030) `maximumResidualUpperPm` is the max over **ACCEPTED** leaves, every one of which is <= budget — which is why EVERY successful patch in every run reports a value a few hundred pm *under* the budget (9,499,3xx at budget 9.5 um; 9,699,0xx at 9.7 um; 19,992,846 at 20 um). It is a decision output. **Any claim quoting `upperPm` as "the mesh's error" is misreading it**; only values well under budget at low depth (e.g. bottom-under 11,530,778 at maxDepth 0, budget 20 um) are real measurements.

**CONSEQUENCE:** the campaign's founding observation is most plausibly this budget-invariant `INCONCLUSIVE`, i.e. a decision-procedure edge at the depth cap on cells sitting on the bisector — NOT a 1e7-1e8-cell Clarke subdivision blow-up. Whether it is a certifier defect (bound saturating just above whatever threshold is tested) or a genuine undecidable-at-depth-24 cell is the open question; it needs a read of the decimal kernel's max-depth consult path, which was out of scope here. Until that is settled, **S1 (pivot+defect node rule) has no measured problem to solve**: bubble certifies, and web's failure is not shown to be Clarke slack.

**SCOPE CAVEATS (honest):** inner-wall failures in this harness are partly a tessellation artifact — the source probe uses a `rationalStationLadder` for `inner-wall` that this harness omits (bubble inner-wall then fails at 78,673,556 pm, 8.3x over, at the u=0 seam); the OUTER-WALL comparison is the controlled one (identical tessellation, only `v_morph` differs: bubble OK / web INCONCLUSIVE). Single relief 0.04; single pot geometry; no full-pot composed run.

**LEDGER.** NEW (analysis/measurement only, no kernel edit): `research/bridge/_strataVoronoiCertify.test.ts` (`PF_STRATA_CERTIFY=1`; env `PF_STRATA_MORPH`/`RELIEF`/`MAXDEPTH`/`BUDGET_PM`/`ALOG2`/`VLOG2`/`DEADLINE_MS`/`CERTIFY_OUT`), plus a P2 point-probe arm in `research/bridge/_strataFiredMapOverlay.test.ts` (`PF_STRATA_POINTS="u,v;..."`). Runner `vitest.strata.config.ts` (now also includes `_gothicVoronoiConformingSpike.test.ts` for the `PF_SLICE11_VOR_PP` cross-check). Evidence: `research/bridge/out/strata_certify_{bubble,web,web_d30,web_v8,web_b97,web_b20}.txt`. Reused READ-ONLY: `certifyContinuousMappedPatchDistance`, `tessellateAnnularRadialSolidTargetForCertification`, `createFinalArtifactProofSession`, `compileValidatedResidualEvaluator`, `voronoiBisectorSegmentsUv`.

## E-2026-07-23-STRATA001-S0-DENSITY (STRATA-001 S0 increment 3: is the web-mode INCONCLUSIVE a certifier defect, or an honest triangle-budget shortfall?) [MEASURE-ONLY; NO kernel edit]

**HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable):** the budget-invariant `INCONCLUSIVE` found in increment 2 is a certifier DEFECT — a residual bound anchored to whatever acceptance threshold is passed in, rather than a property of the mesh.

**KILL-CRITERION (pre-registered):** defect CONFIRMED iff the failure persists at every budget (no escape) AND the reported overshoot is insensitive to refinement. Defect REFUTED iff a large enough budget certifies AND the overshoot shrinks with depth/density.

**VERDICT: NOT A DEFECT. The certifier is honest; the shortfall is a triangle budget the UNIFORM reference tessellator cannot pay.**

1. **Anchoring disproved by escape.** budget 50,000,000 pm -> outer-wall **OK** (`upperPm=49996373`, 220,276 cells, maxDepth 3). budget 200,000,000 -> **OK**. A budget-anchored bound could never certify.
2. **Mechanism identified.** The b&b throws on the FIRST cell that reaches maxDepth still over budget — a MARGINAL cell, not the worst one. Its bound is `true residual + eps(depth)`; because marginal cells sit right at the acceptance line, the message reads `budget + eps`. That is why an arbitrary non-round budget 9,543,211 pm reports 9,543,233 (**+22**) and 9,400,000 reports 9,400,022 (**+22**) on the SAME triangle 102472 — the offset is the convergence excess, not an anchor.
3. **eps shrinks under refinement, exactly as a converging bound must.** By DEPTH: maxDepth 24 -> 30 gives +23 -> **+1 pm**. By DENSITY: angular/vertical log2 (8,7) -> (9,8) — 65,536 -> 262,144 triangles, 4x — gives +22 -> **+6 pm**. No h-independent plateau anywhere; spec section 3's Clarke-pinning does not occur.
4. **But web mode still misses 9.5 um at the DENSEST tessellation the certifier will accept.** `triangles has 524288 entries; hard snapshot limit is 262144` — (9,9) is rejected outright, so (9,8)=262,144 tri/patch is the ceiling, and there outer-wall is INCONCLUSIVE at 9,500,006 pm: **short by 6 pm on 9,500,000 = 0.6 ppm**.
5. **Bubble certifies at the BASELINE density** (increment 2) — the difference between the modes is purely how much relief detail must be resolved, not a change of mathematical class.

**CONSEQUENCE — the campaign re-points cleanly:**
- **Spec section 5 / phase S1 (pivot + one-sided-defect node rule) is UNFOUNDED.** It exists to guarantee TERMINATION against an h-independent Clarke bound. Measured: the bound converges under both depth and density, bubble certifies, and web is 0.6 ppm short. There is no termination problem to solve.
- **Spec section 4 / phase S2 (conform the partition to the exact kink graph) is VINDICATED and is the actual lever.** Web's failing cells lie ON the order-1 bisector (increment 2: 0.0014 lattice-cell units), which is precisely the graph `voronoiBisectorSegmentsUv` already emits; a uniform tessellator must spend its whole 262,144-triangle allowance everywhere to buy resolution that is only needed on that graph. Conforming spends it where the 6 pm actually lives.

**SCOPE CAVEATS:** outer-wall is the controlled comparison (inner-wall in this harness lacks the source probe's `rationalStationLadder` and fails as a tessellation artifact — 106,697,707 pm at budget 50 um, and RESOURCE_LIMIT at 200 um). Single relief 0.04, single pot geometry, uniform tessellation only — no conforming tessellation was built or tested here.

**LEDGER.** Same instruments as `E-2026-07-23-STRATA001-S0-CERTIFY`; `_strataVoronoiCertify.test.ts` gained `PF_STRATA_MAXCELLS` (cMPD `maxWorkCells`; DEFAULT 1e6 trips at 0 ms on dense tessellations, HARD_MAX 6e6). Evidence: `research/bridge/out/strata_certify_web_dense.txt`.

## E-2026-07-24-STRATA001-S0-CORRECTION (CORRECTS the three S0 rows above: they were run at 50x-reduced relief and are NOT representative) [MEASURE-ONLY; NO kernel edit]

**WHY THIS ROW EXISTS.** The three `E-2026-07-23-STRATA001-S0-*` rows above ran Voronoi at `v_relief 0.04` / `v_morph 0`. The REGISTRY DEFAULTS are `v_relief` **2.0 mm** (range 0-5.0) and `v_morph` **1.0 (Web)** — so the measured surface carried **1/50th** of its real relief, in a non-default mode. The parameters were inherited unexamined from `_gothicScreenSlackAudit`'s header comment and `_gothicVoronoiConformingSpike`'s `PF_SLICE11_VOR_PP` probe. Caught by Patryk: at that amplitude the features are near-tolerance by construction, and a uniform grid "generalizes them to a bumpy grid" rather than representing them.

**RE-MEASURED AT REGISTRY DEFAULTS (`v_relief 2.0`), uniform tessellation, budget 9.5 um:**

| config | outer-wall | previously reported |
|---|---|---|
| `v_relief 0.04`, bubble, (8,7) | OK 9,499,530 | "certifies in 99 s" |
| **`v_relief 2.0`, bubble, (8,7)** | **INCONCLUSIVE** 9,500,023 | — |
| **`v_relief 2.0`, web, (8,7)** | **INCONCLUSIVE** 9,500,024 | — |
| **`v_relief 2.0`, web, (9,8) = 262,144 tri/patch cap** | **INCONCLUSIVE** 9,500,009 | — |

Additional patches also fail at real relief (bottom-top tri=394, top-rim tri=7424) which never failed at 0.04.

**WHAT IS RETRACTED.** "Bubble certifies end-to-end / the hang does not exist" (row `S0-CERTIFY` finding 1) is **VOID** — it certified a de-featured surface. Every "bubble is fine" statement in the three rows above inherits that defect. The site-cone refusal census (128 cells) and the fired-map overlay percentages were also measured at 0.04 relief and must be re-run before being cited.

**WHAT SURVIVES (re-verified at `v_relief 2.0`).**
1. **No h-independent Clarke plateau.** maxDepth 24 -> 30 still moves the bound **9,500,024 -> 9,500,001 pm** at REAL relief, exactly as at 0.04. The validated screen converges; spec section 3's "subdivision cannot close it" remains refuted at production amplitude.
2. **`targetToMeshUpperPm` is max over ACCEPTED leaves** (cMPD:1025-1030), hence <= budget by construction — a code fact, unaffected by parameters. Never quote it as the mesh's error.
3. **The b&b throws on the FIRST cell reaching maxDepth over budget** — a marginal cell, not the worst — which is why the message reads `budget + eps`.

**THE ACTUAL FAILURE, RESTATED.** Voronoi cannot be certified by the **uniform** reference tessellator at ANY legal density: at the hard `262144` tri/patch snapshot cap it is still short (+9 pm at real relief, +6 pm at 0.04). Triangles are spent evenly across the domain while the residual lives on the bisector graph. **This is a triangle-PLACEMENT failure, not a screen failure.**

**THE STANDARD TO MATCH (`GothicArches_p1_H32_OD30_certified.stl`, 304,808 tris).** Its certified path (`PF_GOTHIC_STL`, spike :1000-1064) is NOT a dense uniform grid — it is a **coarse** base (`angularDivisionsLog2 8`, `verticalDivisionsLog2 5` = 256x32) plus `angularStations`/`verticalStationsByPatch` (`rationalStationLadder`) plus **`conformingChordsByPatch: gothicChordsForPatch(...)`** on both walls. The ~18x triangle multiplier over the base grid is spent ON the arch creases. That is feature representation; a uniform grid at 4x the density is not.

**THE GAP FOR VORONOI.** `voronoiBisectorSegmentsUv` already emits the exact order-1 bisector geometry (dyadic sites => exact lines), but there is **no chord assembly** — `voronoiBisectorGuides.ts:16-17` states it outright: "Grid-station snapping and chord-chain assembly for conformingChordsByPatch are the next increment." That unbuilt increment is spec section 4 / plan S2 Task 2.2 (`assembleVoronoiConformingChords`). **Phase S2, not S1, is the work.**

**OPEN CONCERN FOR THE WHOLE CERTIFIED CORPUS.** The Gothic exemplar itself used `gaRelief: 0.2` against a registry default of **1.5** (7.5x reduced). If the standard is full fidelity at parameters users can actually dial, the certified corpus needs an audit of which configs were certified at reduced relief — the same defect this row corrects, potentially sitting in prior rows.

**LEDGER.** Same instruments; `_strataVoronoiCertify.test.ts` `PF_STRATA_RELIEF` (default 0.04 retained only for continuity with the rows above — **pass 2.0 for representative runs**). Registry defaults read from `src/styles/registry.ts:355-366` (Voronoi) and `:183-190` (GothicArches).

**ADDENDUM — the reduced relief is IN THE CERTIFIED ROSTER, not just in my run.** `research/bridge/_certRoster.ts:149-163` (verbatim from `CERTIFIED_POTS` in `annularSolidReferenceTessellation.test.ts`, the PF_G2_POT gate's own roster):

```
name: 'Voronoi_H32_OD30_bubble',
styleParams: { v_morph: 0, v_relief: 0.04 },     // defaults are 1.0 (Web) and 2.0 mm
divisions: { angularDivisionsLog2: 8, 'outer-wall': 7,
             verticalStationsByPatch: { 'inner-wall': ... } }   // OUTER WALL: no stations, NO conformingChordsByPatch
```

So the shelf's certified Voronoi (172,032 tris, roster GREEN) certifies a **1/50th-relief, non-default-mode** variant whose **outer wall is a plain uniform grid** — no stations, no conforming chords. My S0 runs reproduced the roster config faithfully; the defect is upstream of this campaign. **`Voronoi_H32_OD30_bubble` is not a meaningful certification of the Voronoi style.**

**Roster relief audit (what "certified" currently means, per style):**

| artifact | relief used | registry default | feature-conforming outer wall? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WaveInterference_defaults_H32_OD30_certified` | **2.3 mm — FULL DEFAULTS** | — | YES (base 2^5 + 288-row rational ladder + fade-kink stations 3/20, 17/20), 1,267,712 tris |
| `GothicArches_p1_H32_OD30_certified` | `gaRelief 0.2` | 1.5 (**7.5x reduced**) | YES (`conformingChordsByPatch` both walls + angular/vertical ladders), 304,808 tris |
| `Voronoi_H32_OD30_bubble` | `v_relief 0.04` | 2.0 (**50x reduced**) + non-default `v_morph 0` | **NO — uniform grid**, 172,032 tris |

**WaveInterference is the existence proof that the goal is reachable at full defaults** — and its method is the same family as Gothic's: coarse base + rational stations/chords placed AT the kinks. Neither exemplar uses a dense uniform grid. **The remaining roster entries need the same relief + conforming audit before any of them is cited as a style-level certification.**
